title: Integrating Inflammation, Pathway Modulation, and Circadian Clock Genes: Conventional and Phytochemical Strategies for Safer Osteoporosis Therapy.
abstract: Osteoporosis is a systemic and silent bone disease that destroys bone microarchitecture, thereby increasing the risk of bone fracture, leading to increased morbidity and mortality. Although it is usually considered a structural deficit, bone remodeling is now fundamentally dependent on the circadian clock, osteoblast cells (responsible for the formation of new bone tissues), osteoclast cells (responsible for breaking down bone tissues), and hormonal rhythms, such as cortisol, melatonin, growth hormone, and parathyroid hormones. Current treatment methods for osteoporosis do not fully restore bone quality and cause many side effects. To address these problems, recent studies have suggested that phytomolecules, as promising therapeutic candidates, can be used for treatment. The use of phytomolecules in combination with conventional treatment, in a time-sensitive manner aligned with circadian biology, is expected to be a better treatment for osteoporosis. Disturbances in the sleep-wake cycle or in neurotransmitter homeostasis dysregulate core clock genes (BMAL-1, CLOCK, PER, CRY) in bone cells, causing instability in bone turnover. Osteochronotherapy involves scheduling the intake of conventional drugs and phytochemicals in accordance with the circadian rhythms of bone cells. This chronobiological method aims to achieve the highest therapeutic efficacy and the lowest toxicity, representing an advanced approach to osteoporosis treatment. In vitro studies have shown that bioactive agents, mainly resveratrol, icariin, genistein, quercetin, and baicalein, have osteoprotective activities with multimodal actions, including antioxidant, anti-inflammatory, and direct effects on RANKL/OPG, AMPK/SIRT1, ESR, NF-κB, and Wnt/β-catenin. The study highlights the importance of incorporating circadian biology into osteoporosis management. The synchronization of therapies with the biological clock can maximize efficiency, reduce adverse effects, and help develop a new approach to bone health. The results emphasize the importance of using phytochemicals as an adjunct therapy, shed light on knowledge gaps in bone remodeling, and suggest possible avenues for utilizing circadian regulation of osteoblasts and osteoclasts to enhance bone density. Furthermore, the incorporation of natural compounds with chronotherapy represents a paradigm shift toward more personalized, safer, and biologically harmonized strategies for osteoporosis therapy. These insights also highlight critical knowledge gaps in bone remodeling research, encouraging future studies to explore how circadian rhythms and neurotransmitter pathways can be leveraged to advance precision medicine in skeletal health. It is now evident that circadian rhythm serves as an important mediator for the maintenance of healthy bones because of its function in bone remodeling. In future research, emphasis must also be placed on exploring the possible differential regulation of osteoclasts and osteoblasts by various circadian rhythms and how such regulation can help enhance bone strength. The review concludes by examining the interplay among neurotransmitter pathways, circadian biology, and sleep quality in relation to conventional and phytochemical interventions.

title: Diurnal Variation in Human Breast Milk: Multi-Omic Characterization and Implications for Infant Circadian Development.
abstract: Components of human breast milk exhibit circadian rhythms that may convey maternal chronobiological signals to infants; however, the diurnal patterns of the milk microbiome and metabolome remain poorly characterized. A cross-sectional study was conducted to assess feeding practices and neonatal sleep patterns in 89 mother-infant dyads. Additionally, 40 breast milk samples were collected from 20 lactating women in a separate cohort at both noon and midnight. Melatonin was measured in all 40 milk samples, microbial composition and metabolites in 13 pairs samples were quantified by LC-MS and metagenomic sequencing. In univariate analysis, neonates receiving mixed feeding demonstrated shorter nocturnal sleep compared to those exclusively breastfed; however, these associations were no longer significant after adjustment for delivery mode. A total of 335,651 microbial features were shared between the noon and midnight samples. Differential abundance analysis identified 20 bacterial genera that differed significantly between the two sampling times. The midnight samples exhibited higher relative abundances of Cognataquiflexum, Segnochrobactrum, and Aquabacterium, with both time points enriched in pathways related to lipid and amino acid metabolism. The noon-midnight differences observed suggest potential implications for infant circadian development. The potential role of circadian-matched breastfeeding strategies in infant development requires further investigation.

title: Perineuronal Nets in Alcohol Use Disorder: Integrating Neuroimmune Activation, Maladaptive Plasticity, and Peripheral Biomarkers. A Critical Review.
abstract: Perineuronal nets (PNNs) are specialized assemblies of the neural extracellular matrix (ECM) which regulate inhibitory circuit function, synaptic stability, and experience-dependent plasticity. This critical review evaluates their emerging role in alcohol use disorder (AUD) by integrating evidence from animal models, human postmortem tissue, neuroimmune studies, peripheral biomarker research, and experimental therapeutics. Alcohol does not induce a uniform pattern of PNN remodeling. Instead, PNN remodeling varies across brain regions and cortical layers and depends on developmental stage, exposure pattern, abstinence interval, sex, and analytical endpoint. Increased or reorganized PNNs may stabilize aversion-resistant drinking and maladaptive alcohol-related memories in cortical and insular circuits, whereas PNN loss in hippocampal and striatal regions may compromise interneuron function, inhibitory control, neurogenesis, and network stability. Human postmortem findings demonstrating layer-specific reorganization of parvalbumin-PNN networks further support the relevance of this framework to AUD. Neuroimmune signaling provides a plausible mechanistic link between alcohol exposure and extracellular matrix remodeling because microglia and astrocytes regulate PNN turnover through inflammatory mediators, oxidative mechanisms, proteases, and phagocytic clearance. The pleiotrophin (PTN)-receptor protein tyrosine phosphatase (RPTP) β/ζ pathway connects PNN organization with glial responses, neuroplasticity, and alcohol-related behaviors, identifying a potential therapeutic entry point. Psychedelic-induced ECM remodeling additionally suggests that transient, controlled windows of plasticity could be paired with behavioral interventions to promote adaptive circuit reorganization. Circulating brevican and neurocan may provide candidate biomarkers of neural ECM remodeling, although their molecular forms, tissue origin, and relationship to brain PNN integrity remain unresolved. Collectively, current evidence positions PNN remodeling as a circuit-specific component of AUD pathophysiology and supports therapeutic and biomarker strategies designed to restore adaptive plasticity while preserving ECM-dependent stability and neuroprotection.

title: Estradiol and working memory: Further evidence for the role of dopamine and COMT gene polymorphism over the menstrual cycle.
abstract: The hormone 17β-estradiol is the dominant form of estrogen in women of reproductive age. Some past work suggests that estradiol may influence women's performance on working memory (WM) tasks that have high executive demands. However, evidence is limited, and the cellular mechanisms that underlie any such effects are largely unknown. Here we used a prospective repeated-measures crossover design to evaluate whether natural variation in estradiol availability over the female ovarian cycle is associated with discernible variations in performance on three neuropsychological tests of WM function. Performance was evaluated during the early follicular phase (low estradiol) and midluteal phase of the cycle (high estradiol). Based on the hypothesis that estradiol-driven variations in dopamine (DA) activity may underlie the effects, we used genotyping to characterize a common allelic variant in the catechol-O-methyltransferase gene (COMT Val158Met) and the dopamine transporter (DAT1 3'-VNTR). Our results showed that menstrual cycle-dependent variation in accuracy was present on all 3 WM tasks, with a medium to large effect size. A significant interaction between high estradiol and COMT genotype was found for Digit Randomization and Spatial Working Memory tests, but no interaction was found on a Self-Ordered Pointing test. In contrast, women's DAT1 genotype moderated the effect of high estradiol on self-ordered pointing. WM accuracy was correlated in a graded manner with the magnitude of the rise in estradiol during the high-estrogen phase. We conclude that brain dopamine activity likely mediates, in part, the impact of 17β-estradiol on WM performance.

title: Predictors of Recovery From Aphasia After Stroke.
abstract: Predicting recovery from aphasia after stroke is challenging, yet essential. Accurate prognoses would enable stroke survivors and families to establish realistic expectations and make informed decisions, allow clinicians to plan rehabilitation, and inform the development and implementation of interventions. This review synthesizes current evidence on predictors of aphasia recovery, integrating diverse biological, behavioral, environmental, and temporal determinants into a unified conceptual framework organized around 3 fundamental determinants: the integrity of the language network, neuroplasticity throughout the remaining brain, and the passage of time. Lesion location and extent are powerful predictors, accounting for more than half of the variance in aphasia outcomes, but other interacting factors contribute to heterogeneous recovery trajectories, including variability in language network organization and effects of diaschisis. The capacity for neuroplasticity depends on the brain health and functionality of surviving tissue, but the realization of this potential depends critically on engagement in language use, which can be promoted by intensive speech-language therapy, social participation and supportive communication environments. Recovery follows a predictable decelerating time course, with rapid early gains driven primarily by reperfusion and resolution of dysfunction in brain regions that support language, and modest but meaningful longer-term improvements deriving from neuroplastic changes. This framework provides a practical heuristic for understanding aphasia recovery, developing clinical prediction tools, and identifying modifiable factors to optimize outcomes.

title: Chemical Profiling and Potential Anti-Inflammatory Mechanism of Gentiana scabra Bunge by UPLC-Q/TOF MS/MS and Network Pharmacology.
journal: Rapid communications in mass spectrometry : RCM
abstract: As a commonly used Tibetan medicine, Gentiana scabra Bunge (GSB) is generally used to clear heat, detoxify the body, and soothe the throat and is indicated for epidemic febrile diseases, cough, laryngitis, pharyngitis, and other symptoms. However, its chemical profiling and mechanism in treating inflammation were not conducted, restricting its clinical applications. This work aimed to reveal the chemical profile and explore the anti-inflammatory mechanism of GSB. UPLC-Q/TOF MS/MS was employed to analyze the chemical constituents in GSB. Network pharmacology was used to predict its anti-inflammatory mechanism. The anti-inflammatory activity of GSB was further evaluated in LPS-stimulated RAW264.7 macrophages by MTT, NO, and Western blot assays. UPLC-Q/TOF MS/MS identified 99 chemical constituents in GSB, mainly 40 iridoids, 36 flavonoids, 11 organic acids, 2 lignans, 5 alkaloids, 3 xanthones, and 2 others, including one potential novel compound and five compounds reported in GSB for the first time. Network pharmacology analysis revealed 355 inflammation-related targets of GSB, with AKT1, TP53, TNF, IL-2, and MAPK as core anti-inflammatory targets, mainly involving the PI3K/Akt, TNF, IL-17, and MAPK signaling pathways. At the cellular level, GSB (0.5-4 mg mL-1) showed no obvious cytotoxicity and significantly inhibited LPS-induced NO production in a concentration-dependent manner but did not significantly suppress LPS-induced MAPK or NF-κB activation. This study provides the first systematic characterization of the chemical information and potential anti-inflammatory mechanism of GSB using UPLC-Q/TOF MS/MS combined with network pharmacology. Although GSB significantly inhibited LPS-induced NO production, it did not significantly suppress MAPK or NF-κB activation, suggesting that its anti-inflammatory effect may involve alternative signaling mechanisms. This study provides a material basis for further mechanistic investigation and clinical application of GSB against inflammatory disease.

title: Natural Antioxidants in Sleep Deprivation: Mechanisms, Therapeutic Potential, and Future Perspectives.
abstract: Sleep Deprivation (SD) is a condition that undermines the body's functional state and is associated with impaired cognition and immunity, dysfunction of the circulatory and metabolic systems, and circadian misalignment. These alterations are accompanied by biologic stress, neuroendocrine imbalance, oxidative stress, and inflammation, affecting both the central nervous system and peripheral organs. Owing to this dual inflammatory and oxidative nature, antioxidant-based interventions have emerged as promising complementary therapeutic approaches. This review summarizes and critically discusses the current evidence on naturally occurring antioxidant compounds and plant extracts with potential protective effects against SD-related pathophysiological alterations, with emphasis on their molecular mechanisms of action and their multifunctional pharmacological properties. Particular attention is given to their antioxidant, antiinflammatory, hypolipidemic, antidiabetic, and cytoprotective activities, as well as their ability to modulate oxidative stress and inflammatory signaling associated with SD. Overall, the available evidence suggests that natural antioxidants may attenuate the deleterious consequences of SD through pleiotropic mechanisms. However, further mechanistic studies and well-designed clinical investigations are required to establish their therapeutic value. In addition to their potential clinical applications, these compounds may provide further insight into the molecular pathways underlying SD pathology and facilitate the development of novel natural therapeutic agents.

title: NLRP3 Inhibition in the Modern Era: Advancing Targeted Pharmacology and Precision Medicine for Cardio-neuroinflammatory Disorders.
abstract: The NLRP3 inflammasome is a crucial component of innate immunity and inflammation, triggering caspase-1 activation and facilitating the maturation and release of pro-inflammatory cytokines such as IL-1β and IL-18. Dysregulated activation of NLRP3 is involved in the pathogenesis of cardiovascular, neurological, and metabolic diseases such as myocardial infarction, heart failure, atherosclerosis, stroke, Alzheimer's disease, and diabetic complications. Thus, the inhibition of NLRP3 could be a potential therapeutic approach for chronic inflammation- associated diseases. This review summarizes the recent advances in the discovery, preclinical evaluation, and clinical translation of NLRP3 inflammasome inhibitors, with a particular emphasis on smallmolecule agents, including MCC950, dapansutrile (OLT1177), NT-0796, and emerging nextgeneration inhibitors. Preclinical and preliminary studies in the early phases of clinical trials suggest that NLRP3 inhibition may lead to inhibition of inflammatory signaling, decrease tissue damage, ameliorate cardiovascular outcomes, and offer neuroprotective properties. In contrast with antiinflammatory drugs with a broad spectrum of activity, selective inhibitors of NLRP3 may have higher mechanistic specificity and greater tolerability. Research is currently directed toward improving blood-brain barrier permeability, reducing off-target effects, identifying NLRP3 variants that are associated with resistance, and incorporating patient stratification by biomarkers to better facilitate precision medicine. Inhibition of the NLRP3 inflammasome is a potential therapeutic target in cardiovascular, neurodegenerative, and metabolic diseases. Ongoing translational research efforts and carefully designed clinical trials are needed to validate their long-term effectiveness, safety, and promise for individualized treatment.

title: Novel Quinazolinone-based CNS-active Agents: In Silico Studies, Synthesis, and In Vivo Evaluation.
abstract: Epilepsy and anxiety disorders remain major neurological challenges despite the availability of several therapeutic agents. However, the long-term use of currently available drugs is often associated with adverse effects, tolerance, and dependence, highlighting the need for safer and more effective therapeutic alternatives. Quinazolinone derivatives have attracted considerable interest as potential Central Nervous System (CNS)-active molecules because of their ability to interact with the GABAA receptor system and modulate neuronal excitability. A series of twelve quinazolinone derivatives (S3D1-S3D12) was designed and subjected to in silico screening using ADME prediction, molecular docking, MMGBSA binding-energy calculations, and molecular dynamics simulations against the GABAA receptor (PDB ID: 4COF). Based on its overall computational performance, the lead compound S3D1 was selected for synthesis and structural characterization using FT-IR, ¹H NMR, ¹³C NMR, and ESI-MS analyses. The pharmacological potential of S3D1 was subsequently evaluated in mice using a PTZ-induced seizure model, the elevated plus maze, rotarod testing, and estimation of the inflammatory cytokines TNF-α and IL-1β. All designed compounds demonstrated acceptable drug-like properties and favorable predicted pharmacokinetic profiles, including predicted blood-brain barrier permeability and compliance with Lipinski's criteria. Among the screened derivatives, S3D1 exhibited the most favorable docking score (-6.82 kcal/mol) and formed favorable interactions with key amino acid residues within the receptor binding pocket. MM-GBSA analysis and molecular dynamics simulations further supported the stability of the S3D1-receptor complex. Experimental studies revealed that S3D1 significantly delayed seizure onset and reduced seizure duration in the PTZ-induced seizure model. The compound also demonstrated anxiolytic activity and effects on motor coordination in the rotarod test. In addition, treatment with S3D1 significantly reduced TNF-α and IL-1β levels, suggesting attenuation of PTZ-induced neuroinflammatory responses. The biological findings were consistent with the computational predictions, suggesting an association between favorable receptor-binding characteristics and the observed pharmacological activity. The presence of the quinazolinone scaffold, amide linker, and 2,4-difluorophenyl moiety may contribute to the observed activity by promoting favorable receptor interactions and physicochemical properties compatible with CNS penetration. The reduction in pro-inflammatory cytokine levels further suggests that the compound may exert its pharmacological effects through mechanisms involving the modulation of inhibitory neurotransmission and attenuation of neuroinflammatory processes. The present study identified S3D1 as a promising quinazolinone-based lead compound with significant anticonvulsant and anxiolytic activity, as well as effects on PTZ-induced motor impairment and reductions in measured pro-inflammatory cytokine levels. The combined computational and experimental findings support the potential of S3D1 for further investigation as a quinazolinone-based lead candidate for epilepsy and related CNS disorders.

title: Effects of Vitamin D on Immune System Function and Cognitive Performance in Homeostasis, Experimental Autoimmune Encephalomyelitis (EAE), and Multiple Sclerosis (MS).
abstract: Vitamin D, historically recognized for its role in calcium and bone metabolism, has evolved into a multifunctional neuroimmunomodulatory hormone with considerable effects on the Central Nervous System (CNS) and immune modulation. Growing evidence suggests that vitamin D affects both innate and adaptive immune responses by modulating the activity of Macrophages (MQ), Dendritic Cells (DCs), T lymphocytes, B lymphocytes, and microglial cells. Additionally, vitamin D signaling via the Vitamin D Receptor (VDR) modulates various biochemical pathways associated with inflammation, oxidative stress, neuronal survival, and neuroprotection. These processes have garnered significant interest in neuroinflammatory and neurodegenerative conditions, especially Multiple Sclerosis (MS). Experimental and clinical research indicate that vitamin D insufficiency correlates with heightened vulnerability to multiple sclerosis, exacerbated disease activity, disruption of the blood-brain barrier (BBB), oxidative damage, and diminished remyelination. Furthermore, vitamin D facilitates neurogenesis, regulates neurotrophic factors, promotes oligodendrocyte maturation, and modulates dopaminergic neurotransmission. Recent data underscores its possible involvement in cognition, neuropsychiatric function, and neurodevelopmental processes. This study offers an extensive examination of vitamin D's physiology and metabolism, its immunomodulatory and neurobiological mechanisms, and its significance in MS etiology and cognitive function. The essay additionally examines the therapeutic potential of vitamin D supplementation, existing limits of clinical evidence, and safety risks associated with high-dose delivery. The existing evidence collectively indicates a significant role for vitamin D in neuroimmune regulation.

title: Single-Device Bidirectional Photonic Synapses: From Polarity Switching to Adaptive Neuromorphic Computing.
abstract: Neuromorphic vision requires hardware capable of integrating sensing, memory, and computation with bidirectional information processing. Single-device bidirectional photonic synapses (BPS), which enable positive and negative photoresponses within the same physical element, provide a compact platform for adaptive photonic computing. However, the diverse architectures, regulation strategies, and physical mechanisms reported for BPS have hindered systematic understanding and quantitative comparison. Here, we establish a unified Structure-Regulation-Mechanism-Function (S-R-M-F) framework to organize single-device BPS from device architecture and polarity regulation to physical mechanisms, synaptic functions, quantitative benchmarks and neuromorphic applications. We further distinguish physical photoresponse polarity from its functional interpretation in synaptic computing and highlight key considerations including energy consumption, reproducibility, variability, and system-level scaling. Finally, we identify the transition from empirically observed PPC-NPC switching toward predictive, deterministic, programmable and reproducible operation as a key direction for future BPS development, with physics-informed modeling and closed-loop control offering promising routes toward adaptive photonic neuromorphic hardware.

title: New-onset cognitive impairment after delirium among hospitalised older Ghanaians: A Pilot Study.
abstract: Delirium is a potentially modifiable risk factor for dementia. However, post-delirium cognition has hardly been studied in Africa, where the burden of both disorders is rising disproportionately. We estimated the incidence of new-onset cognitive impairment (NCI) 6 months after hospitalisation with non-stroke delirium among older Ghanaians. This was a prospective observational pilot study conducted among 60 previously cognitively unimpaired (retrospective proxy assessment) adults aged ≥60 years, hospitalised with non-stroke prevalent delirium in a Tertiary Hospital. Delirium was confirmed and rated using the Confusion Assessment Method (CAM) and Severity Scale (CAM-S) within 24-72 hours of admission and reassessed twice weekly during hospitalisation, and at 6-week, 3- and 6-month follow-up visits. NCI was defined as Identification and Interventions for Dementia in Elderly Africans Study Cognitive Test (IDEA) score <8/15 + CAM-negative at 6 months. Demographic, clinical and psychosocial data were collected at baseline. We calculated the cumulative incidence function for NCI, accounting for competing mortality risk and right censoring due to dropout. We analysed predictors of NCI using Fisher's exact test and Firth regression, and mortality using Cox proportional hazards regression. The cumulative incidence of NCI was 22.4% (95% CI: 8.0-36.8%). Mortality was 42.3% (95% CI: 26.2-58.3%). NCI was associated with advanced age (≥80 years; p=.001). Mortality was associated with CAM-S at enrolment (HR: 1.153; 95% CI: 1.020-1.303), mean CAM-S during hospitalisation (HR: 1.423; 95% CI: 1.261-1.605), hyperactive delirium (HR: 2.632; 95% CI: 1.119-6.188) and frailty at 6 weeks (HR: 1.817; 95% CI: 1.001-3.297). In this pilot cohort of older Ghanaians hospitalized with delirium, NCI and mortality were common by 6 months. Longitudinal studies of post-delirium cognitive outcomes in diverse African cohorts are feasible and necessary, but future research should incorporate design, sampling and analytical measures to address survivor bias.

title: Oncogenic Ppm1d mutations deregulate the p53 pathway in primary mouse gliomas.
abstract: High-grade gliomas such as diffuse midline glioma (DMG) are incurable brain tumors with limited treatment options. A subset of high-grade gliomas harbor somatic, truncating mutations in exon 6 of phosphatase PPM1D, which stabilize the protein and deregulate p53 signaling. However, the consequences of these mutations for tumor initiation, progression, and therapy remain unclear. We developed a conditional Ppm1d-loxP-exon6-loxP-exon6-E518X-tag mouse allele (Ppm1d-flex-6) that enables lineage-, spatial-, and temporal-specific expression of a glioma-derived truncated Ppm1d protein from its endogenous locus in the presence of Cre-recombinase. Ubiquitous activation of mutant Ppm1d was modeled using the Meox2-Cre driver, and primary gliomas were modeled using the RCAS/tv-a system to introduce Cre and PDGFB co-drivers into Nestin-positive neural stem cells. Complementary studies were performed in mouse embryonic fibroblasts (MEFs) expressing truncated Ppm1d following Cre recombination. While Meox2-Cre-driven ubiquitous recombination of Ppm1d-flex-6 produced muted phenotypes, Ppm1d-flex-6 recombination in Nestin+ neural stem cells accelerated gliomagenesis. Its oncogenic effect was weaker than complete p53 loss, and it did not accelerate tumorigenesis further in p53-null tumors. Single-cell RNA-sequencing revealed that Ppm1d-flex-6 gliomas adopt more progenitor-like transcriptional states and upregulate p53- and cell cycle-associated pathways. In MEFs, Ppm1d-flex-6 enhanced proliferation and shifted transcriptomic programs toward MAPK and PI3K-Akt signaling, while impairing DNA damage responses, including reduced γ-H2AX induction after irradiation. These defects sensitized cells to radiation and decreased clonogenic survival after ionizing radiation and PARP inhibition. Ppm1d mutations confer intermediate suppression of the p53 pathway, consistent with the clinical features of PPM1D-mutant gliomas and are associated with radiosensitivity and PARP inhibitor vulnerability.

title: Metabolic reprogramming in neurofibromatosis type 1: Plasma metabolomic signatures of MEK inhibition.
abstract: Neurofibromatosis type 1 (NF1) is a tumor predisposition syndrome driven by RAS/MAPK hyperactivation due to neurofibromin loss. Although selumetinib has changed the management of inoperable plexiform neurofibromas (PNs), the systemic metabolic changes associated with NF1, PN burden, and MEK inhibition remain poorly understood. We aimed to identify circulating metabolomic signatures associated with NF1, tumor status, and selumetinib treatment. We conducted a monocentric observational study at IRCCS Istituto Giannina Gaslini (Genoa, Italy). Seventy-five participants aged 3-30 years were enrolled in 4 age- and sex-matched groups: NF1 patients with inoperable PNs receiving selumetinib (≥4 cycles), NF1 patients with untreated PNs, NF1 patients without tumors, and healthy controls. Peripheral plasma samples were analyzed by high-resolution mass spectrometry-based metabolomics. Data processing was performed with MS-DIAL and MS-FINDER, followed by statistical analysis with Bonferroni correction. Pathway enrichment was assessed using KEGG and MetaboAnalyst 6.0. Distinct metabolomic profiles emerged across groups, with the largest differences observed in selumetinib-treated patients. Compared with untreated PN patients and healthy controls, treated patients showed downregulation of pathways related to central carbon metabolism and upregulation of amino acid-related pathways. Additional alterations involved lipid metabolism and mitochondrial-associated processes. Neurofibromatosis type 1 patients without tumors showed fewer metabolic changes. Overall, PN status and MEK inhibition appeared to be the main drivers of systemic metabolic variation. Selumetinib therapy in NF1 is associated with a distinct plasma metabolic signature, consistent with reduced proliferative energy metabolism and activation of adaptive amino acid and mitochondrial pathways. These findings support metabolomic profiling as a potential noninvasive tool for treatment monitoring and biomarker development in NF1-associated tumors.

title: Digital Anhedonia Revisited: Reward Processing and Clinical Implications.
abstract: Digital anhedonia was proposed to describe diminished enjoyment of offline experiences in the context of sustained digital engagement. Its subsequent appearance in public mental health writing and scholarly discussion creates an opportunity to clarify the concept and its evidentiary requirements. This editorial revisits selected newer findings and applies established reward-processing concepts to comparisons of online and offline pleasure within the same person. Problematic social media use should not, by itself, be interpreted as evidence of anhedonia. The studies reviewed do not directly demonstrate this pattern or establish that digital engagement causes reduced offline pleasure. I propose examining four related dimensions: anticipated pleasure, willingness to expend effort, reward learning, and pleasure during participation. Clinical assessment should establish change from previous functioning and consider apathy, executive difficulty, fatigue, mood, sleep, medications, and limitations affecting access to rewarding activities. Repeated assessments in daily life could test whether a reproducible pattern exists, while behavioral tasks and selected neuroimaging studies could investigate its behavioral and neural correlates. Neural findings would require interpretation alongside subjective experience and functioning. Digital health development should prioritize recovery of participation and enjoyment in meaningful activities. Digital anhedonia remains a hypothesis whose value depends on demonstrating explanatory and clinical usefulness.

title: Multiscale computation in psychoradiology for developmental psychiatric disorders: a conceptual framework.
abstract: Developmental psychiatric disorders like attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder (ADHD) and autism spectrum disorder (ASD) remain difficult to characterize and treat, mainly due to significant clinical heterogeneity and a lack of objective biomarkers. Conventional neuroimaging often fails to distinguish etiology from correlation and lacks the insights for actionable molecular targets, as most rely on cross-sectional correlations. Here, we present a conceptual framework for multiscale computation that proceeds from longitudinal imaging-marker discovery to cross-scale mechanistic hypothesis generation and molecular imaging-assisted evaluation of interventions. Emotional dysregulation as a transdiagnostic dimension and related research in ASD and ADHD as illustrative cases are used to demonstrate the application of this framework. We first demonstrate how longitudinal trajectory algorithms can identify predictive imaging biomarkers, using developmental deviations in the inferior frontal gyrus and insula associated with emotional dysregulation and related symptoms as illustrative examples. We then describe multiscale fusion models (mFusion) that integrate multiomics data, including genetics, transcriptomics, and positron emission tomography (PET), to link neuroimaging markers to candidate molecular pathways, illustrated by findings implicating pathways related to excitatory-inhibitory balance and GABAergic signalling in ADHD and ASD. Finally, we highlight the integration of magnetic resonance spectroscopy into clinical trials for intervention-based evaluation, using changes in insular γ-aminobutyric acid (GABA) associated with clinical improvement in ASD as an example. Together, these approaches provide a conceptual framework for progressing from imaging-marker discovery towards mechanistic and therapeutic translation.

title: Chronic traumatic encephalopathy: neurodegenerative disease or scientific misadventure of the 21st century?
abstract: Chronic traumatic encephalopathy theory of the 21st century suggests that repetitive impacts to the head cause precipitates of cortical tau, which then become the substrate for mental health problems and the nidus for a spreading tauopathy. Each of these lacks empirical scientific support, but for complex reasons the lay public and much of the neuroscience community now favor the pathogenic sequence: sport initiates an insidious neurobehavioral syndrome some years after retirement, which proceeds inexorably to degenerative dementia. A close look at the literature, however, discloses pervasive misinterpretation and over-interpretation of case material, unwieldy consensus articles, clinical disease claims based on circular logic, and misrepresentation of classical literature, such that the narrative as a whole is tantamount to science fiction insofar as a clinical meaning is concerned. Continued challenge from the neuropathology community and attention to scientific philosophy are needed, both to preserve the integrity of the neuropathology discipline and to avoid iatrogenic effects on the health of society.

title: PTC-assisted sustainable synthesis and integrated in silico evaluation of novel 2-oxo-nicotinonitrile derivatives as multitarget larvicidal agents against Culex pipiens L.
abstract: This study reports an operationally efficient and mild phase-transfer catalytic (PTC) synthesis of novel 2-oxo nicotinonitrile derivatives as potential larvicidal agents against Culex pipiens L. Compared with conventional reflux, the PTC protocol afforded markedly higher yields of 73-95% within 6-10 h, whereas the thermal method gave only 16-23% yields after 19-24 h. Larvicidal evaluation against third-instar larvae identified compounds 8, 2b, 10, and 4 as the most active derivatives, with LC50 values of 7.65, 9.92, 10.48, and 10.48 µg mL-1, respectively. Although their potency was lower than that of pyriproxyfen, these compounds showed promising activity as newly synthesized lead candidates. Molecular docking against Lymnaea stagnalis acetylcholine-binding protein and Aedes aegypti juvenile hormone-binding protein revealed favorable interactions consistent with a possible multitarget mode of action. DFT calculations showed that compound 8 possessed the lowest HOMO-LUMO energy gap and hardness and the highest softness among the synthesized candidates, supporting its superior activity within the series. SAR analysis highlighted the importance of molecular rigidity, substituent size, and hydrogen-bonding capacity. Compounds 4 and 8 also showed favorable predicted ADME and toxicity profiles, including lack of blood-brain barrier penetration, acceptable bioavailability, and relatively high LD50 values. Overall, PTC provides an operationally efficient and high-yielding route to biologically active nicotinonitrile derivatives, with compound 8 emerging as the most promising larvicidal lead.

title: Gut microbiome dysbiosis as a convergent contributor of neurodegenerative disease: unifying mechanistic pathways and emerging precision microbiome-directed therapies.
abstract: Neurodegenerative diseases (NDDs) are increasingly recognized as systemic disorders shaped by the microbiota-gut-brain axis. Within this framework, gut microbiome dysbiosis is better defined by reproducible modules of functional imbalance than by isolated taxonomic shifts. These aberrant microbial networks transmit peripheral signals to the central nervous system through three interconnected routes: immune-inflammatory activation, metabolic reprogramming, and aberrant vagal and humoral neural transmission. Because peripheral inputs may converge on shared downstream pathways within the brain, they can drive mitochondrial decompensation, oxidative stress, and pathological protein aggregation. This review integrates current evidence into a conceptual framework describing how host-microbiome interactions may contribute to neurodegeneration and then critically appraises microbiome-targeted interventions, including dietary modulation, next-generation probiotics, and fecal microbiota transplantation. Moving from correlation-based reasoning toward a causal, mechanism-driven account, we argue for patient stratification and outline a path toward precision microecological therapies against NDDs.

title: Research on the multilevel pathogenesis and cross-scale correlation networks of the microbiota-gut-brain axis in mediating central nervous system disorders.
abstract: The microbiome-gut-brain axis (MGBA) is a bidirectional communication network that contributes to organismal homeostasis through neural, endocrine, immune, and microbial metabolic signaling. The gut microbiota influences central nervous system (CNS) function through pathways involving the vagus nerve and circulation, with metabolites such as short-chain fatty acids and tryptophan derivatives regulating neurogenesis, barrier integrity, and immune responses. Conversely, the CNS modulates the intestinal environment through the autonomic nervous system and the hypothalamic-pituitary-adrenal axis, thereby influencing gut barrier function and microbial composition. Disruption of this regulatory network may initiate a cascade of pathological changes, linking microbial metabolic alterations and cellular dysfunction to intestinal barrier impairment, systemic inflammation, blood-brain barrier disruption, and altered brain function. Such MGBA disturbances have been associated with CNS disorders. This review synthesizes five core communication mechanisms of the MGBA and examines how their interactions across molecular, cellular, tissue, organ, and systemic levels may contribute to CNS pathology. By framing CNS disorders as dynamic processes involving cross-scale network imbalance, this review provides an integrated perspective on MGBA-related disease mechanisms and highlights directions for targeted intervention.

title: Increased functional connectivity in glioma: separating compensation from tumor-promoting remodeling.
abstract: Increased functional connectivity (FC) in glioma is often interpreted as compensatory neuroplasticity or tumor-promoting circuit remodeling, although FC is a measure of coupling rather than a mechanism. We propose a qualitative framework that first examines whether the measurement is suitable for the claim, then evaluates evidence for patient function and tumor behavior separately. The two lines of evidence are combined only when they concern the same patient context, anatomical compartment, metric, and time course. The framework also distinguishes maladaptive or excitability-related remodeling from tumor promotion. Human longitudinal studies associate network restoration with recovery, whereas experimental cancer neuroscience shows that neural activity and neuron-glioma synapses can promote malignant behavior. Increased FC should therefore be reported with its modality, metric, comparator, compartment, disease phase, reliability, and prespecified outcomes before being interpreted as compensatory, maladaptive, or tumor-promoting.

title: Effects of combined palmitoylethanolamide and probiotics on behavior and hippocampal and colonic gene expression in 12-month-old mice exposed to chronic stress.
abstract: To evaluate the effects of combined palmitoylethanolamide (PEA) and three probiotics (Lactobacillus rhamnosus LA801, Lactobacillus helveticus LA102 and Bifidobacterium longum LA101) in middle-aged mice exposed to chronic unpredictable mild stress (CUMS), a model that reflects the transitional stages of aging associated with late-life depression. Twelve-month-old male C57BL/6J mice received a daily supplementation of PEA (5 mg/kg) and probiotic strains (2 × 109 CFU in total) or vehicle for 10 weeks, starting 7 days before the initiation of an 8-week CUMS protocol. Behavioral tests were conducted after CUMS protocol. Underlying mechanisms were investigated by analyzing the expression of genes in the colon and hippocampus at study endpoint, in mice that were then 14.5 months old. PEA and probiotic supplementation significantly reduced specific CUMS-induced anxiety-like behaviors and increased locomotion in comparison with CUMS-exposed control group. Results suggest a more moderate CUMS-induced increase in corticosterone levels and showed hippocampal Nr3c1 upregulation, a key mediator of glucocorticoid signaling. In the hippocampus, supplementation markedly decreased Il6 expression, increased glial-associated markers expression (Gfap, Iba1) and promoted genes involved in plasticity and neurogenesis (Bdnf, Syn1 and Syp). In addition, supplementation modulated monaminergic gene expression. At the colonic level, supplementation increased Ocln and Il10 expression while reducing Il6 expression. Although the PEA and probiotic combination produced limited behavioral improvements in middle-aged mice exposed to chronic stress, it was associated with coordinated transcriptomic changes in both peripheral and central tissues. The modulation of pathways related to inflammation, pro-resolving responses, neuroplasticity, and neurotransmission provides mechanistic support for further investigation of this intervention as a candidate approach to counteract alterations associated with chronic stress and late-life depression.

title: Neuronal homeostasis as feedback control: a framework for localizing regulatory dysfunction in neurodevelopmental disorders.
abstract: Neurons preserve functional activity despite continual changes in synaptic drive, morphology, and membrane protein turnover. This stability is commonly attributed to homeostatic regulation. There is converging evidence that neurodevelopmental disorders (NDDs) may arise from failure of this regulation. Here, we formulate neuronal homeostasis as a negative-feedback control problem comprising a regulated variable, set point, sensor, controller, and effectors. This formulation converts broad claims of impaired homeostasis into mechanistically distinct hypotheses. Dysfunction may arise from sensor miscalibration, a displaced set point, defective controller transduction, incorrect gain, or saturation or loss of an effector's adjustability. We use this framework to reinterpret evidence from NDDs in which diverse genetic lesions converge on altered excitability, excitatory-inhibitory balance, and circuit stability. The framework yields two central conclusions. First, homeostatic dysfunction should often be direction-specific rather than uniformly deficient, because upward and downward compensation rely on partially separable molecular and physiological mechanisms. Second, electrophysiological measurements are insufficient to identify the governing regulatory rule as degeneracy permits distinct ion-channel configurations to support similar activity, whereas integral feedback allows the same electrophysiological measurements to arise from different regulatory dynamics. Consequently, localizing dysfunction within the loop requires bidirectional perturbations, longitudinal measurement, and computational models that represent a population of models rather than a unique set of parameters. A control-theoretic framework therefore provides both a mechanistic taxonomy and an experimental strategy for determining how neuronal regulation fails in disease.

title: Structural localization of antisocial behaviours in patients with behavioural variant frontotemporal dementia.
abstract: Behavioural variant frontotemporal dementia (bvFTD) is frequently associated with new-onset antisocial and criminal behaviours, occurring in up to 92% of bvFTD patients and presenting as an initial symptom in up to 14% of patients. Despite their frequency and severity, the structural brain changes underlying antisocial behaviour in bvFTD remain unclear. Work in FTD and other populations suggests that antisocial behaviours can be further differentiated into aggressive and rule-breaking behaviours, which may have distinct neural mechanisms. In the current study, we tested the hypothesis that aggressive and rule-breaking antisocial behaviours would differentially relate to cortical volume in regions implicated in both antisocial behaviour and bvFTD, including the orbitofrontal/ventromedial prefrontal cortex (OFC/vmPFC), anterior temporal lobe (ATL) and anterior insula (AIns). Structural MRI scans were acquired from bvFTD patients (n = 45, mean age: 63.2 ± 8.7 years, 22% female) and age-matched healthy controls (n = 31, mean age: 63.3 ± 8.4 years, 80% female). Antisocial behaviour was measured using the Social Behaviour Questionnaire (SBQ), which provides subscores for aggressive and rule-breaking behaviours. We examined associations between brain volume and antisocial behaviours using region-of-interest and whole-brain voxel-wise approaches, controlling for age, sex and intracranial volume. To determine the effects of brain atrophy on connected regions, we also applied atrophy network mapping, which identifies regions functionally connected to atrophied regions using single-subject atrophy maps and a normative connectome derived from resting-state functional connectivity in 1000 healthy individuals. Increased antisocial behaviours were associated with greater left (P = 0.02) and right (P = 0.01) OFC/vmPFC volume, but not with ATL or AIns volume. These anatomical associations were specific to aggressive but not rule-breaking behaviour. Comparison with healthy controls demonstrated that this positive association between antisocial behaviour and brain volume was due to mild atrophy, rather than normal or increased cortical volume in the OFC/vmPFC. Atrophy network mapping revealed that antisocial behaviour was associated with less atrophy in locations within OFC/vmPFC-centred networks and with atrophy in functionally anti-correlated networks. In contrast, atrophy within networks anti-correlated with the precuneus/posterior cingulate cortex was associated with decreased antisocial behaviour. Our results suggest that antisocial and aggressive behaviours in bvFTD are associated with a complex pattern of mild OFC/vmPFC atrophy coupled with atrophy in anti-correlated networks, which may lead to functional dysregulation within OFC/vmPFC-centred networks.

title: Relationship Between Gut Microbiota and Serum Metabolites in Patients With Tinnitus.
abstract: The role of the gut mycobiome and its interaction with bacteria remains unexplored in tinnitus. We aimed to characterize the gut fungal community, its associated serum metabolites, and inter-kingdom network stability in chronic tinnitus. Case-control study. A single-center study conducted in a university hospital. We performed a multi-omics analysis on 70 patients with chronic tinnitus and 30 healthy controls. Fecal samples underwent fungal ITS sequencing, and plasma was analyzed using untargeted liquid chromatography-mass spectrometry (LC-MS) metabolomics. We integrated these data sets with bacterial data to construct co-abundance networks and develop multi-kingdom diagnostic models. Patients with tinnitus exhibited significant fungal dysbiosis, with reduced diversity and enrichment of opportunistic genera, including Malassezia. Fungal alterations correlated with distinct serum metabolite profiles and predicted dysregulation of neurotransmitter and neural membrane pathways. Strikingly, we observed a profound collapse of the fungal-bacterial interaction network in the tinnitus cohort. A diagnostic model integrating fungal and bacterial biomarkers demonstrated outstanding predictive accuracy (area under the receiver operating characteristic curve [AUC] = 0.978). This study provides the first evidence of gut mycobiome dysbiosis in tinnitus, establishing fungi as a critical component of the gut-brain-ear axis. The observed collapse in inter-kingdom network stability points to a broader ecosystem-level dysfunction beyond single-kingdom alterations.

title: Polysaccharides in the treatment of brain injury-related diseases: blood-brain barrier limitations and peripheral action pathways.
abstract: Natural polysaccharides possess outstanding advantages including low toxicity, favorable biocompatibility, and multi-target regulatory capabilities. They hold broad application prospects in neuroprotective research on Alzheimer's disease (AD) and depression. Owing to their high molecular weight and strong hydrophilicity, intact polysaccharides cannot readily cross the blood-brain barrier (BBB). Only a minor proportion enters the systemic circulation after oral administration. However, even under conditions of extremely low intracerebral exposure, polysaccharides still exhibit significant central neuroprotective effects. The underlying mechanism is that intact polysaccharides primarily act as fermentation substrates for gut microbiota, which then promote the production of short-chain fatty acids (SCFAs) and modulate tryptophan and bile acid metabolism. These peripheral metabolites, upon entering the circulation, further regulate peripheral immune responses and the activity of the hypothalamic-pituitary-adrenal (HPA) axis, improve neurotrophic signaling and redox homeostasis, and transmit signals to resident immune cells within the central nervous system via central boundary structures. Therefore, natural polysaccharides do not directly enter the brain. Instead, they exert neuroprotective effects via a cascade pathway involving the gut microbiota-peripheral metabolites-immune and humoral network. This article systematically elaborates on its multi-pathway mechanisms of action and summarizes adjunctive brain-targeted delivery approaches, including pathology-dependent modulation of BBB permeability and brain-targeted delivery. Future research should further elucidate the causal relationships among various signaling pathways, strengthen quality control and clinical trials, and facilitate their translational application.

title: Effects of Tai Chi exercise on homocysteine, limbic system, and attention control in cerebral small vessel disease.
journal: Frontiers in cell and developmental biology
abstract: Elevated homocysteine (Hcy) is a risk factor for mild cognitive impairment in cerebral small vessel disease (CSVD-MCI), but the underlying neural pathways remain unelucidated. The limbic system is vulnerable to Hcy-related damage and plays a critical role in attention control; however, the Tai Chi-associated relationship in Hcy, limbic structures, and attention control has not been examined in CSVD-MCI. We therefore conducted cross-sectional and longitudinal analyses to (1) explore the relationship between Hcy, limbic system structural and functional properties, and attention control, and (2) test whether Tai Chi exercise improves attention control via limbic pathways. Baseline (N = 58) and post Tai Chi exercise evaluations (N = 31) were conducted in patients with CSVD-MCI. We measured serum Hcy levels, regional structural properties and regional fractional amplitude of low-frequency fluctuations (fALFF), and attention control. Partial correlation and mediation analysis were conducted to examine relationships between Hcy levels, structural and functional properties in core limbic regions, and attention control at baseline in individuals with CSVD-MCI. Changes in the above variables and their relationship after Tai Chi exercise were examined using ANCOVA and partial correlation. Finally, we examined whether Tai Chi exercise moderated the relationship between changes in structural and functional properties in core limbic structures and attention control. At baseline, a relatively higher level of Hcy was indirectly associated with impaired attention control through reduced cortical thickness in the right parahippocampal gyrus. Tai Chi exercise improved attention control and significantly changed fALFF relative to the control group. Notably, Tai Chi-related functional changes in the bilateral caudate and right parahippocampal gyrus underlie attention control improvement. This study reveals a potential vascular-neurobiological pathway centered in the limbic system involving cortical thinning and functional compensation, which could be modulated by Tai Chi exercise and the related attention control improvement in CSVD-MCI.

title: Prediction of One-Week Sport-Related Concussion Symptom Severity Using the Sport Concussion Assessment Tool and CogState Brief Battery.
abstract: The recovery from sport-related concussion (SRC) is highly heterogeneous, with many individuals experiencing symptoms that persist beyond typical recovery periods. Early identification of individuals at risk of prolonged symptoms is critical to inform timely interventions and set recovery expectations. Although acute symptom burden is one predictor of future symptoms, reliance on self-reported measures limits objectivity and reduces clinical utility. This prospective cohort study evaluated the discriminatory accuracy of the CogState Brief Battery, alone and in combination with the Sport Concussion Assessment Tool (SCAT), to classify Australian football players with SRC from those without at 24 h, and to determine whether these measures were predictive of the presence and severity of symptoms at one week. Adult amateur Australian football players (n = 181) were recruited following SRC (n = 109, 86% male) or a noninjured match (n = 72, 90% male) to complete the CogState Brief Battery, SCAT, and Rivermead Post Concussion Questionnaire at 24 h and one week. Area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC) analyses quantified the accuracy of 24-h CogState performance and SCAT symptom severity to distinguish SRC from controls. Additional models evaluated whether combining 24-h symptom severity assessments with CogState performance improved prediction of one-week symptom burden and symptomatic status. SCAT symptom severity demonstrated excellent classification accuracy for SRC at 24 h (AUC [95% CI]: 0.949 [0.916-0.981]). CogState task performance showed lower accuracy but demonstrated fair classification and prognostic utility. Poorer CogState performance at 24 h was associated with greater overall symptom severity at both 24 h and one week, and with symptom severity across individual symptom domains. Twenty-four-hour symptom severity and CogState performance independently contributed to prediction of symptomatic status at one week post-SRC (e.g., Identification task AUC [95% CI]: 0.721 [0.606-0.835]. These findings indicate that CogState performance at 24 h may provide objective information that complements subjective symptom reporting, supporting both diagnosis and early prognostication in the clinical evaluation of SRC.

title: Young people at risk of suicide. Ecological momentary assessment and digital safety planning in a case series.
abstract: Young people remain at high risk of recurrent suicidal behavior following a suicidal crisis, highlighting the need for innovative strategies to support post-crisis care. Digital interventions, including Ecological Momentary Assessment (EMA) and digital Safety Planning, may facilitate continuous monitoring and personalized support during this vulnerable period, describing the feasibility, acceptability, and clinical trajectories associated with EMA and digital Safety Planning across heterogeneous intervention exposures. We present a case series of four participants enrolled in the RCTs SmartCrisis-Teen and SmartCrisis 2.0 cohorts following a recent suicidal crisis. Clinical evolution, engagement with the digital platform, EMA data, use of the digital Safety Plan, and user satisfaction are described throughout follow-up. Clinical trajectories were heterogeneous. One participant experienced a suicide attempt during follow-up, whereas no further suicide attempts were recorded in the remaining participants. All participants remained engaged in specialized mental health care. EMA captured short-term fluctuations in suicidal ideation, sleep, and emotional functioning, although these patterns did not consistently coincide with clinical events. This case series provides preliminary evidence supporting the feasibility and acceptability of combining EMA with a digital Safety Plan as an adjunct to standard psychiatric care following a suicidal crisis. Although clinical effectiveness cannot be established from this descriptive case series, these findings support the potential clinical utility of digital monitoring and safety planning and justify further evaluation in larger prospective controlled studies.

title: Extracellular vesicle miRNAs, NOS/NO homeostasis, and NLRP3 inflammasome signaling in schizophrenia-related cognitive impairment: a mechanistic review and testable hypothesis.
abstract: Cognitive impairment is a major determinant of poor functional recovery in schizophrenia, but the molecular events connecting neuroimmune disturbance, redox imbalance, and synaptic dysfunction remain incompletely understood. Studies in patients have reported altered extracellular vesicle microRNA (EV-miRNA) profiles, abnormalities in nitric oxide synthase/nitric oxide (NOS/NO)-related markers, and altered or increased microglial expression of NLRP3 inflammasome-associated proteins. These findings point to possible convergence among EV-mediated signaling, redox regulation, and inflammasome activity, yet they do not define a continuous causal pathway. This review examines evidence from patient studies, patient-derived and schizophrenia-related models, and mechanistic work in other disease contexts to assess a putative EV-miRNA-inflammatory transcriptional network-NOS/NO-NLRP3-synaptic/cognitive impairment framework. We emphasize several evidentiary boundaries: EV-miRNA expression changes should be distinguished from functional intercellular delivery, predicted targets should not be treated as validated mechanisms, and peripheral molecular associations cannot by themselves establish pyroptosis in the brain. The framework also highlights the context dependence of NO-related effects, particularly their reliance on the redox microenvironment, and separates cytokine maturation and release, GSDMD-mediated pore formation, and pyroptotic cell death as related but distinct downstream events. Future studies should determine whether source-defined EV-miRNAs directly regulate NOS/NLRP3 signaling, whether these molecular changes precede longitudinal cognitive decline, and whether intervention or rescue experiments can demonstrate causal links across the pathway. Integrating source-resolved EV profiling, multi-omics analysis, and clinical follow-up may clarify whether combined molecular indicators can support cognitive stratification and risk prediction in schizophrenia.

title: Editorial: Temporal perception and memory: dynamic interactions.
Stimulus-driven leakage in naturalistic neuroimaging.
abstract: This article elucidates a methodological pitfall of cross-validation for evaluating predictive models applied to naturalistic neuroimaging data-namely, "stimulus-driven leakage." While this problem is well known as "leakage in training examples" in machine learning, it may be difficult to detect in practice due to conventions in neuroscience. Stimulus-driven leakage can occur when predictive modeling is applied to data from a conventional neuroscientific design, characterized by a limited set of stimuli repeated across trials and/or participants. It results in spurious predictive performance due to overfitting to repeated signals, even in the presence of independent noise. Through comprehensive simulations and real-world examples, following a theoretical formulation, the article underscores how such data leakage can occur and how severely it can compromise results and conclusions when combined with widespread informal reverse inference. The article concludes with practical recommendations for researchers to avoid stimulus-driven leakage in their experimental design and analysis.

title: A deep-learning microglial response score integrates single-cell and spatial transcriptomics for Alzheimer's disease stratification.
abstract: Microglia exhibit diverse responses in Alzheimer's disease (AD), yet linking these responses to tissue pathology and disease heterogeneity remains challenging. We aimed to develop a deep-learning microglial response score (DL-MRS) integrating single-cell, spatial and bulk transcriptomics to characterize AD-associated transcriptional patterns. We analyzed human single-cell, spatial and bulk transcriptomic data to characterize microglial clearance and inflammatory programs. These programs and tissue-context features formed eight module-level inputs to a multilayer perceptron that generated DL-MRS. Model performance and feature contributions were assessed using five repeats of five-fold cross-validation, cross-cohort testing, feature-set comparisons and SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP) analysis. Spatial localization, individual-level prediction using spatial transcriptomic data, and molecular heterogeneity within AD were also examined. Single-cell analyses characterized clearance-enriched and inflammation-enriched microglial groups. Descriptive spatial projection visualized regional variation in the weighted microglial and tissue-context programs. Across 697 AD and control bulk samples, DL-MRS achieved a repeated out-of-fold area under the receiver-operating characteristic curve (AUC) of 0.939 and a mean cross-cohort transfer AUC of 0.947. SHAP analysis of the expanded model identified complement as the largest contributor, alongside contributions from microglial and tissue-context modules. Among 129 AD samples, median DL-MRS was higher in the immune-enriched than in the neuronal/synaptic-enriched molecular group (0.970 versus 0.800). These findings support DL-MRS as an interpretable research tool for integrating microglial and tissue-context signals to characterize AD-associated transcriptional patterns and within-disease molecular heterogeneity. DL-MRS integrates microglial and tissue-context signals into an interpretable measure of AD-associated transcriptional remodeling. By capturing coordinated variation across immune, glial, vascular, neuronal and synaptic programs, DL-MRS reveals molecular heterogeneity among AD samples and provides a framework for investigating interindividual differences and advancing molecular stratification in AD research.

title: AI and mixed reality in child and adolescent psychiatry: where we were, where we are, and where we are headed.
journal: Frontiers in child and adolescent psychiatry
abstract: Children and adolescents are the first generation to grow up in the era of integration of artificial intelligence and augmented reality (AR) into daily life, yet they are largely absent from the evidence base for the immersive technologies most likely to help them with their mental health challenges. This Perspective explores history of the field from early laboratory AR systems for simple phobias, through randomized trials of augmented reality exposure therapy on commercial headsets, to current platforms in with generative AI agents that animate spatially mapped characters for patients' experience of in vivo interactions. Augmented reality is potentially better matched to youth than virtual reality: the child remains in their own environment, on their own feet, in continuous visual contact with clinician and the caregiver, while feared social and physical stimuli are introduced under graded control. Because these platforms are transdiagnostic and function based, targeting impaired or avoided human interaction rather than a single diagnosis, they extend across anxiety disorders, post-traumatic stress disorder, autism spectrum disorder, early psychosis, and school refusal, and offer an opportunity for standardized, behavioral assessment. There also risks specific to minors: AI-facilitated avoidance, engagement-optimized models that might validate distorted threat appraisal, cultural and developmental bias in AI-generated social behavior, and assent and data governance requirements. The pediatric evidence base is empty because the studies have not been attempted, and filling it requires immersive-technology infrastructure for both research and clinical care in child and adolescent psychiatry, and a generation of clinicians and investigators trained to use it.

title: Tolerability, administration burden, and patient-reported experience of riluzole formulations in ALS: a longitudinal real-world study.
abstract: Riluzole is available as tablets (T), oral suspension (OS), and orodispersible film (OF), but comparative real-world data on tolerability, administration burden, and patient-reported experience are limited. In this longitudinal study, 138 patients with amyotrophic lateral sclerosis (ALS) were evaluated at baseline (79 OF, 21 OS, 38 T) and 97 were reassessed after a median of 3.9 months. OS-treated patients had longer disease duration and greater functional impairment than OF or T (p < 0.001), reflecting preferential use in more advanced disease. Oral numbness was more frequent with OF than OS or T (54.4% vs. 14.3% vs. 13.2%; p < 0.001) and decreased during follow-up (42.3%-28.9%; p = 0.016), partly because patients reporting it switched away from OF. OF use (adjusted OR 10.55 vs. T, p < 0.001) and female sex (OR 2.59, p = 0.035) were independently associated with higher, and older age with lower, odds of an adverse event at baseline (OR 0.43 per 10-year increment, p < 0.001); at 3-month follow-up, OF remained the strongest formulation-related predictor (OR 5.42, p = 0.024), while an adverse event already present at baseline was itself the strongest predictor of one at follow-up (OR 5.11, p = 0.006). Dysphagia was associated with tablet manipulation (OR 7.19, p = 0.034). Differences among formulations concerned packaging convenience and independent self-administration rather than overall satisfaction, and lower disease severity was weakly associated with higher satisfaction regardless of formulation (ρ = 0.21, p = 0.015). Formulation persistence among reassessed patients was high (85.6%), and most patients who left OF had anticipated this intention at baseline. The three riluzole formulations are used in clinically distinct ALS populations and differ in tolerability and usability rather than overall satisfaction, and a prior adverse event marks persisting risk. Formulation choice should be individualized and periodically reassessed as disease progresses.

title: The Empoli REMS after five years: a single-centre retrospective observational cohort study of patient characteristics and time to exit.
abstract: Evidence on time to exit from Italian Residences for the Execution of Security Measures (REMS) and its clinical and forensic correlates remains limited. This study described patients admitted during the first five years of activity of the Empoli REMS and estimated time to permanent exit. This single-centre retrospective observational cohort included all 34 patients admitted between 22 July 2020 and 31 July 2025. Descriptive analyses used the full cohort. Two patients with a recorded stay of 0 months were excluded from time-to-event analyses. Permanent exit from the Empoli REMS was the event; patients still admitted at study end were right-censored. Kaplan-Meier estimates, log-rank tests, Cox models, and Benjamini-Hochberg false-discovery-rate correction were used. The sample was predominantly male (n = 30, 88.2%), with a mean age of 37.4 years (SD = 10.9); schizophrenia-spectrum disorders were the most frequent diagnoses (n = 19, 55.8%). The time-to-event cohort included 32 patients, with 13 exits and 19 censored observations. Observed follow-up was 20.1 months (SD = 13.3), and the Kaplan-Meier median time to exit was 24 months (95% CI: 19 months to not reached). A homicide-related index offence (HR = 0.19, 95% CI: 0.06-0.67, p = .009) and each additional 12 months of court-ordered security measure duration (HR = 0.38, 95% CI: 0.18-0.77, p = .008) were associated with a lower exit hazard; both associations remained significant after false-discovery-rate correction. No statistically significant associations were detected for migrant status, LAI treatment, or history of illicit drug use; however, the corresponding estimates were imprecise and the confidence intervals did not exclude potentially meaningful associations. Within this small exploratory cohort, time to exit was associated primarily with offence-related and judicial variables. The findings require confirmation in larger multicentre cohorts.

title: Targeting STAT5 abrogates survival signaling and sensitizes chronic lymphocytic leukemia cells to BCL-2 and MCL-1 inhibition.
abstract: STAT5 is constitutively activated in several hematologic malignancies, where it promotes cell survival. In chronic lymphocytic leukemia (CLL), although STAT5b levels are elevated in leukemic cells from CLL patients compared with healthy controls, the functional significance and mechanistic role of STAT5 remains poorly understood. In this study, we knocked down both STAT5A and STAT5B using lentivirus-mediated shRNA. Loss of STAT5 significantly inhibited CLL cell viability and induced apoptosis. Mechanistically, STAT5 depletion markedly attenuated the activation of the pro-survival AKT and ERK signaling pathways and reduced the expression of the anti-apoptotic proteins MCL-1 and BCL-2, indicating that STAT5 is important for CLL cell survival and represents a potential therapeutic target. Consistently, pharmacological inhibition of STAT5 with the small-molecule compound AC-4-130 significantly suppressed cell viability and promoted apoptosis in CLL cells, accompanied by diminished AKT and ERK signaling and reduced MCL-1 and BCL-2 expression. Furthermore, AC-4-130 in combination with the BCL-2 inhibitor ABT-199 or the MCL-1 inhibitor A-1210477 induced greater CLL cell apoptosis in a dose- and patient-dependent manner. Collectively, these findings demonstrate that STAT5 confers a survival advantage on CLL cells and that its depletion or inhibition triggers apoptosis, providing a preclinical rationale for testing STAT5 inhibitors in combination therapy for CLL.

title: Longitudinal profiling of putative SCFA-associated gut taxa and sodium butyrate epithelial assays in acute myeloid leukemia.
journal: Frontiers in cellular and infection microbiology
abstract: Intensive therapy for acute myeloid leukemia (AML) disrupts intestinal homeostasis, but the relationship between microbial composition and epithelial injury remains uncertain. We analyzed 508 longitudinal stool samples from 67 patients using patient-clustered models, conducted an exploratory microbiome Mendelian randomization (MR) screen and host-gene annotation, and evaluated sodium butyrate (NaB) in chemotherapy-injured epithelial and inflammatory cell assays. None of 1,521 MR tests passed false-discovery-rate correction. Host annotation identified a 17-gene candidate module. Putative short-chain fatty acid (SCFA)-associated taxa had lower relative abundance on days 15-28 than before chemotherapy. Patients with diarrhea had lower full-follow-up minimum abundance of these taxa (Cliff's delta = -0.518; 95% CI, -0.738 to -0.268; P = 1.20 x 10-4; q = 0.00180). C. difficile positivity was associated with greater maximum single-genus pathobiont relative abundance (q = 0.0261), but this association did not survive a fixed-window median sensitivity analysis. Period estimates were similar after adjustment, while small pre-event matched analyses did not show temporal precedence. NaB partially improved Caco-2 barrier readouts and was associated with lower THP-1 p-SYK/SYK and Caco-2 p-NF-kappaB/NF-kappaB ratios. Longitudinal taxonomic associations and NaB-responsive cell phenotypes provide complementary evidence. They do not establish butyrate depletion, microbial causality, receptor dependency, a continuous host pathway, or clinical efficacy.

title: Inhabiting a wounded world: a qualitative phenomenology of ecological anxiety.
abstract: Ecological anxiety is defined as distress caused by awareness of the ongoing climate crisis. This qualitative phenomenological study aimed to describe how lived experience is altered in ecological anxiety. We conducted 58 interviews with 30 participants who identified themselves as experiencing ecological anxiety. Interviews combined lifeworld analysis with a micro-phenomenological approach to explore specific experiential episodes. Transcripts were analyzed using constructivist grounded theory, with participant validation and intercoder verification. Participants reported fatigue, rumination, bodily symptoms, and sleep difficulties, alongside feelings of guilt, shame, and anger and heightened empathy toward humans and non-human entities. We identified two forms of ecological anxiety: informational, involving distress associated with information about the climate crisis, and experiential, arising from witnessing its consequences. A central phenomenological characteristic was a marked attitude toward information, including a perceived obligation to remain informed despite the associated distress. Participants also described altered temporality, feeling alienated from the future and rushed in the present. These temporal disturbances were intertwined with a pervasive loss of agency. Our findings suggest that ecological anxiety extends beyond discrete episodes of worry to broader alterations in participants' lifeworlds, which we conceptualized as a prereflective sense of inhabiting a wounded world. Within this predominantly European, highly educated sample, ecological anxiety also provided a framework for interpreting wider personal and societal concerns. These findings highlight the importance of considering informational, temporal, and social dimensions when understanding and addressing ecological anxiety.

title: EFECT enables reliable and reproducible stochastic simulations across disciplines.
abstract: Stochastic simulations underpin computational research in fields from systems biology and epidemiology to finance and physics-informed machine learning, yet their reproducibility is hard to quantify because each run yields different outcomes. Existing practices to improve computational reproducibility focus on sharing code, simulation seeds, data, and software environments but do not ensure independent reproduction of results, limiting scientific rigor. Here we introduce the Empirical Characteristic Function Equality Convergence Test (EFECT), a universal computational framework for quantifying the statistical reproducibility of stochastic simulations based on empirical characteristic functions. EFECT defines a normalized EFECT error that measures distributional differences between two sets of simulation outputs over a model- and scale-independent range, and an EFECT convergence point that specifies the minimum sample size required to achieve a desired reproducibility threshold at a chosen significance level. EFECT applies to any simulation whose results can be represented as bounded, real-valued data, regardless of modeling formalism or source of stochasticity. To facilitate widespread adoption and data exchange, we implemented EFECT in an open-source software library and a compact, machine-readable standardized report. We rigorously evaluated the framework across more than 40 test cases spanning stochastic differential equations, agent-based models, Boolean networks, and partial differential equations. Applying EFECT to published models in pandemic epidemiology, financial stochastic volatility, and physics-informed neural networks reveals that commonly used sample sizes are often underpowered: substantial parameter differences can go undetected unless thousands of replicates are simulated. By providing a domain-agnostic statistical reproducibility metric, reusable software libraries, and a standardized report format, EFECT offers a practical framework for embedding quantitative reproducibility and replicability checks into stochastic simulation workflows across data-intensive disciplines. Thus, EFECT delivers the capability to make scientific inferences and policy decisions on the basis of reliable, reproducible stochastic simulations.

title: Hearing loss as an inference problem: sensory precision, conversational repair, and partner adaptation.
abstract: Conversational understanding is often approached as a problem of successful signal transmission. This paper develops a complementary account in which conversation is treated as a reciprocal process of inference and action: interlocutors must infer the latent causes of one another's signals, estimate the reliability of the available evidence, and act to keep uncertainty sufficiently manageable for coordinated exchange. Hearing loss provides a theoretically revealing case for understanding conversation as reciprocal inference because it perturbs the generative process through which speech causes produce auditory observations, while also increasing the importance of contextual inference, precision control, conversational repair, and partner adaptation. We develop an active inference framework with three principal contributions. First, we distinguish the sensory perturbation produced by hearing loss from the listener's generative model representation of that perturbation through reduced, redistributed, or potentially miscalibrated likelihood precision. Second, we differentiate compensatory precision control, delayed commitment, covert repair, and overt conversational repair, treating overt repair as an epistemic policy whose value depends on expected information gain, prior preferences, learned policy habits, and interpersonal consequences. Third, we extend the framework beyond the isolated listener by formalising how interlocutors infer one another's states, select partner-sensitive policies, and update partner models through repeated interaction.
