The proposal therefore connects foundational questions with a clinically and socially consequential sensory condition. Rather than treating hearing loss solely as an individual perceptual deficit, it examines how altered sensory evidence changes the coupled inferential dynamics through which listeners and communication partners jointly maintain understanding. The framework generates empirically discriminating predictions and outlines how these can ultimately be evaluated through model comparison, behavioural and physiological measures, dyadic interaction paradigms, and longitudinal research. Overall, the proposal recasts hearing-impaired conversation as the joint regulation of uncertainty under asymmetric sensory and interpersonal constraints.

title: Consensus-Based Diagnostic Criteria for Parsonage-Turner Syndrome/Neuralgic Amyotrophy: A Modified Delphi Study.
abstract: Parsonage-Turner syndrome (PTS), also known as neuralgic amyotrophy (NA), is an acute-onset peripheral neuropathy predominately affecting the upper extremity and causing substantial pain and disability. No formal international consensus-based diagnostic criteria exist, contributing to diagnostic delays, inconsistent terminology, and limited ability to collate and systematically analyze data. This study aimed to develop consensus-based diagnostic criteria and a diagnostic algorithm for PTS/NA. A modified Delphi study was conducted with an international, multidisciplinary panel of experts selected based on clinical and research experience with PTS/NA. A steering committee drafted preliminary statements informed by a literature review and panelist-derived diagnostic challenges across 9 domains. Two electronic survey rounds used Likert-scale and binary response formats, with consensus defined as ≥ 75% agreement or disagreement. All 13 panelists completed both rounds (100% response rate). Of 86 items, 52 (60%) reached agreement. The panel endorsed "Parsonage-Turner syndrome" and "neuralgic amyotrophy" as interchangeable terms. Classic PTS/NA was defined by acute-onset severe pain (≥ 7/10) and severe weakness in a non-myotomal distribution. Non-classic presentations warranted confirmatory electrodiagnostic testing and/or nerve-focused imaging. Hourglass-like nerve constrictions were considered likely pathognomonic (100% agreement). If steroids were considered, early initiation was recommended in classic presentations, even before confirmatory testing. These criteria may shorten time to diagnosis, standardize terminology, guide resource utilization, and facilitate clinical trials. Future research should prioritize validation of the criteria in patient cohorts.

title: Task-Oriented Co-Design of Optoelectronic Synaptic Devices: From Physical Mechanisms to System Integration.
abstract: Optoelectronic synaptic devices integrate optical sensing, state storage, and conductance modulation, offering high bandwidth, ultrafast response, and low energy consumption. These capabilities enable the development of energy-efficient, scalable intelligent vision systems with rich synaptic plasticity, making optoelectronic synaptic devices one of the most promising approaches for overcoming the limitations of conventional von Neumann computing architectures. However, existing studies often evaluate device performance and synaptic functions under disparate structures and operating conditions, obscuring the relationships among physical mechanisms, device design, and task requirements, and limiting the establishment of generalizable design principles. This Review presents a task-oriented framework that connects biological functions and application requirements with physical mechanisms, multilevel hardware design, and system integration. We first summarize biological synaptic and retinal functions and define key evaluation metrics and task requirements. We then discuss major operating mechanisms and strategies for coordinated optimization across materials, interfaces, device structures, and arrays. Representative applications are further reviewed, together with key challenges, including device stability, array uniformity, large-scale integration, peripheral-circuit overhead, and standardized benchmarking. By shifting the focus from isolated performance optimization toward cross-level co-design, this Review provides design guidelines for reproducible, scalable, and energy-efficient optoelectronic neuromorphic hardware.

title: FOXM1-induced TRIM9 inhibits neutrophil extracellular traps formation to attenuate cerebral I/R injury via STING/AMPK axis.
abstract: Cerebral ischemia-reperfusion (I/R) injury is a major challenge in stroke management, with neutrophil extracellular traps (NETs) playing a key role in exacerbating damage. This study aimed to elucidate the function and mechanism of FOXM1 in cerebral I/R injury. A mouse middle cerebral artery occlusion (MCAO) model and an oxygen-glucose deprivation/reoxygenation (OGD/R) model in bEnd.3 endothelial cells were established. NETs formation was assessed by detecting MPO-DNA complexes, H3Cit, and neutrophil elastase. Inflammatory cytokines were evaluated using RT-qPCR, and protein stability was assessed by cycloheximide chase assay. Molecular interactions were examined using chromatin immunoprecipitation (ChIP), co-immunoprecipitation (Co-IP) and dual luciferase reporter assay. FOXM1 was downregulated following I/R. FOXM1 overexpression reduced infarct volume, edema, and NETs formation in MCAO mice. In vitro, FOXM1 upregulation attenuated endothelial injury in OGD/R-stimulated bEnd.3 cells and decreased the release of NETs markers. Mechanistically, FOXM1 directly bound to the promoter of TRIM9 and activated its transcription. TRIM9 subsequently promoted K48-linked ubiquitination and degradation of HMGB1, thereby influencing STING/AMPK signaling and reducing NETs formation. Knockdown of either TRIM9 or FOXM1 partially reversed the effects of HMGB1 depletion on NETs formation. FOXM1 overexpression ameliorated cerebral I/R injury by enhancing TRIM9 expression, which suppressed NETs formation through HMGB1-modulated STING/AMPK signaling.

title: Engineered MSC-Derived Nanovesicles Delivering Cascade-Responsive Self-Assembling Gd-Based Contrast Agents for Enhanced T2-Weighted MRI of Glioblastoma.
abstract: The clinical management of glioblastoma (GBM) remains severely constrained by the blood-brain barrier (BBB), which impedes both diagnostic and therapeutic interventions. Here, we present an innovative bioengineered platform (hMSC-NV-Gd-CBT) based on human mesenchymal stem cell-derived nanovesicles (hMSC-NVs) that are covalently modified with a self-assembling, small-molecule Gd-based contrast agent (N3-Gd-CBT). These nanovesicles retain the inherent BBB-penetrating capacity of their parent cells while offering substantially higher production yields than conventional hMSC-derived exosomes. Furthermore, the incorporation of glutathione/cathepsin B (CTSB) cascade-responsive self-assembling probe N3-Gd-CBT enables tumor-specific aggregation and accumulation of contrast agents, significantly enhancing T2-weighted MRI contrast in GBM. Systematic evaluation at 9.4 T reveals that hMSC-NV-Gd-CBT generates superior MRI contrast for GBM compared with the free N3-Gd-CBT probe, hMSC-NV-Gd-CBT co-treated with a CTSB inhibitor, and commercial Gd-DTPA. This strategy not only provides a novel diagnostic tool for brain tumors and other neurodegenerative diseases but also opens new avenues for developing next-generation T2-weighted MRI contrast agents.

title: A Deep Quantitative Proteome Turnover Platform for Human iPSC-Derived Neurons.
abstract: Quantitative evaluation of protein turnover in human neurons is crucial for understanding neuron homeostasis and guiding drug development for neurological diseases. However, measuring protein turnover in postmitotic neurons remains challenging because of the broad dynamic range of neuronal protein half-lives and limited proteome coverage in SILAC (stable isotope labeling by amino acids in cell culture) experiments. Here, we established a comprehensive analytical platform for protein turnover measurements in human induced pluripotent stem cell (iPSC)-derived neurons by integrating optimized dynamic SILAC labeling, extensive offline peptide fractionation, data-independent acquisition (DIA) LC-MS/MS, and a streamlined computational workflow with stringent kinetic modeling and filtering criteria. As a result, this platform enabled the quantification of 10,792 apparent protein half-lives from 162,854 unique peptides, substantially expanding the coverage of low-abundance regulatory proteins and therapeutically relevant targets, including 72% of the human kinome, 45% of FDA-approved drug targets, and 72% of potential drug targets. Comparative analyses of glutamatergic cortical neurons and spinal motor neurons revealed globally conserved proteome dynamics alongside subtype-specific differences in protein turnover and abundance. To maximize the accessibility and utility of these datasets, we developed NeuronProfile (https://www.neuronprofile.com/), an interactive resource for exploring protein turnover, abundance, protein copy number, peptide-level kinetics, subcellular localization, and therapeutically relevant proteins in human neurons. Together, this work establishes a robust analytical platform and community resource for quantitative studies of neuronal proteostasis, therapeutic target prioritization, and neurological disease research.

title: Proteomic Investigation of Serum Biomarkers for Early Neurological Prognosis in Patients Undergoing Extracorporeal Cardiopulmonary Resuscitation: A Prospective Multi-Center Pilot Study.
abstract: Extracorporeal cardiopulmonary resuscitation (ECPR) has emerged as a promising intervention for refractory cardiac arrest; however, predicting neurological outcomes remains challenging. This study aimed to identify early prognostic biomarkers for neurological outcomes in ECPR patients using comprehensive proteomic profiling. In this multi-center prospective cohort study, serum samples were collected at 0, 24, 48, and 72 hours after ECPR and analyzed by high-resolution liquid chromatography-tandem mass spectrometry. Among 1,135 quantified proteins, differential expression was defined by |log₂ fold-change| ≥ 1 and P < 0.05. Twenty-two patients were enrolled and stratified by 90-day Cerebral Performance Category (CPC) scores: good neurological outcome (CPC score 1-2, n = 15) and poor neurological outcome (CPC score 3-5, n = 7). Proteomic analysis suggested distinct temporal expression patterns and potential differences in key proteins between neurological outcome groups. Four proteins associated with neuronal function or neuroinflammation, including GRN (24 hours), S100A6 (0 hours), PRDX6 (48 hours), and PTPRF (24 hours, 48 hours), showed numerically greater discriminative performance than neuron-specific enolase (NSE). Their areas under the receiver operating characteristic curve were 0.857, 0.833, 0.821, and 0.821, respectively, compared with 0.800 for NSE at 48 hours. In this preliminary study, GRN, S100A6, PRDX6, and PTPRF exhibited improved discriminative performance compared with NSE, suggesting their potential as promising serum proteomic biomarkers for early neuroprognostication after ECPR. While these exploratory findings warrant validation in larger cohorts, they establish a compelling foundation for the development of next-generation, biomarker-based models to guide clinical management in ECPR patients.

title: [METTL14-mediated m6A modification regulates osteoblast response to mechanical signals].
journal: Sheng li xue bao : [Acta physiologica Sinica]
abstract: This study aims to investigate the response pattern of methyltransferase-like 14 (METTL14) to mechanical signals in osteoblasts and the underlying molecular mechanisms by which it mediates mechanical signal transduction. Various mechanical stimulation models, including simulated microgravity using a clinostat, hypergravity, and fluid shear stress (FSS), were employed to detect METTL14 expression changes in osteoblasts via Western blot. Alkaline phosphatase (ALP) staining and RT-qPCR were utilized to evaluate the regulatory effects of METTL14 on osteoblast differentiation and Piezo-type mechanosensitive ion channel component 1 (Piezo1) mRNA stability. Furthermore, a simulated microgravity mouse model was established via hindlimb unloading (HU), which was combined with bone tissue samples from clinical osteoporosis patients to explore the correlation between METTL14 expression and the pathological process of bone loss. The results showed that in osteoblasts treated with clinostat-simulated microgravity, METTL14 expression and N6-methyladenosine (m6A) modification levels decreased synchronously; conversely, hypergravity and FSS stimulation upregulated METTL14 expression and enhanced osteoblast function. Western blot analysis revealed that METTL14 protein levels were significantly reduced in the bone tissues of HU mice, and consistently low expression was also observed in the clinical osteoporosis patient samples. Additionally, METTL14 expression increased in a time-dependent manner during osteogenic differentiation. Overexpression of METTL14 promoted osteoblastic differentiation, whereas its knockdown significantly inhibited this process. Mechanistic studies demonstrated that METTL14 enhances Piezo1 mRNA stability via m6A modification, thereby promoting the phosphorylation of downstream cAMP response element-binding protein (Creb) and osteoblast differentiation. In conclusion, METTL14 can sensitively perceive changes in mechanical signals and participate in the regulation of osteoblast differentiation and the development of unloading-induced bone loss through the "METTL14-Piezo1-m6A" epitranscriptional regulatory axis. This study provides a novel perspective for elucidating the molecular mechanisms of bone metabolic disorders under space microgravity and pathological conditions.

title: [Chaihu Guizhi decoction ameliorates simulated spaceflight-induced depression by modulating the gut microbiota and gut microbial-derived metabolites].
journal: Sheng li xue bao : [Acta physiologica Sinica]
abstract: This study aims to investigate the effect of Chaihu Guizhi decoction (CGD) on simulated spaceflight-induced depression and the underlying mechanisms associated with intestinal flora. Hindlimb unloading (HU) mice were used as simulation models to recreate the specific environment of spaceflight. Behavioral tests were used to demonstrate the depression-like behaviors. The gut microbiota and gut microbial-derived metabolites were characterized by 16S rRNA gene sequencing and untargeted metabolomics, respectively. The serum metabolites were investigated by HM700 metabolomics. The results showed an increase in depression-like behavior in HU mice compared with control mice, and CGD enhanced the cognitive function in HU mice by regulating brain neurotransmitter levels and inhibiting neuronal injury. CGD treatment markedly altered the gut microbiota and gut microbial-derived metabolites in HU mice, and the differences in metabolites were correlated with fluctuations of the gut microbiota. Additionally, serum metabolomics analysis revealed that CGD regulated the serum metabolites in HU mice, including the abundances of tryptophan and aspartic acid. CGD modulated the gut microbiota and fecal metabolites toward a more favorable profile and improved brain function, thereby protecting neurons and counteracting HU-induced injury. These findings suggest that CGD has a preventive effect on simulated spaceflight-induced depression through modulation of the gut microbiota and gut microbial-derived metabolites.

title: Design, Binding Profiles, and Therapeutic Potential of Imidazole- and Benzimidazole-Containing Cholinesterase Inhibitors: A Review.
abstract: Cholinesterase enzymes, specifically acetylcholinesterase (AChE) and butyrylcholinesterase (BChE), play a central role in regulating cholinergic neurotransmission. In neurodegenerative conditions such as Alzheimer's disease (AD), a significant imbalance occurs: AChE activity declines by up to 67% in key brain regions like the hippocampus and temporal lobe, whereas BChE expression increases by up to 165%. Consequently, dual- or targeted inhibition of AChE and BChE remains a pivotal strategy in neuropharmacology to restore synaptic acetylcholine levels, manage cognitive decline, and alleviate symptoms in related neuromuscular conditions like myasthenia gravis. Although FDA-approved therapeutics (such as donepezil, rivastigmine, and galantamine) offer symptomatic relief, their clinical utility is frequently limited by peripheral cholinergic adverse effects and disease progression, driving the search for novel structural classes. Recently, imidazole- and benzimidazole-bearing scaffolds have gained significant traction as versatile structural modules in inhibitor design. Owing to their unique hydrogen-bonding capacity, basicity, and electronic characteristics, these heterocyclic cores participate in key noncovalent interactions within the catalytic and peripheral anionic sites of both enzymes. This review provides a comprehensive compilation of imidazole- and benzimidazole-containing cholinesterase inhibitors, detailing their structural design strategies, enzyme binding mechanisms, and key molecular docking interactions to provide a valuable framework for the rational development of next-generation anti-Alzheimer therapeutics.

title: Motor neuron disease due to a novel PIK3R1 mutation.
abstract: Mutations in PIK3R1, which encodes the regulatory subunit (p85α) of class I phosphoinositide 3-kinase (PI3K), are associated with immunologic and developmental disorders, but their effects on the nervous system have not been studied. We identified a novel heterozygous frameshift mutation (PIK3R1 c.1710dup) in a patient with common variable immunodeficiency who developed adult-onset, slowly progressive ALS-like motor-neuron disease. Studies of patient-derived induced pluripotent stem cells (iPSCs) demonstrated PIK3R1 haploinsufficiency with selective AKT activation. Investigation of patient's iPSC-derived motor neurons (iMNs) showed reduced neuronal electrical activity, and markedly increased apoptosis. Single-cell RNA sequencing revealed coordinated up-regulation of differentiation and apoptosis programs across neuronal and glial clusters. Engineering the PIK3R1 c.1710dup mutation into healthy-control iPSCs reproduced the impaired electrical activity, increased apoptosis, and transcriptional vulnerability, confirming the variant's cell-intrinsic pathogenicity. In contrast, introduction of canonical APDS2-associated PIK3R1 splice mutations into the same genetic background did not produce these abnormalities, establishing a variant-class-specific mechanism of PI3K dysfunction. Together, these findings define PIK3R1 c.1710dup as a distinct pathogenic variant that links PI3K-pathway dysregulation to human motor-neuron degeneration and expands the mechanistic spectrum of PIK3R1-associated disease.

title: Smoking Very Low Nicotine Content Cigarettes Produces Measurable Cardiovascular and Autonomic Effects: Evidence Informing FDA-Proposed Reduced Nicotine Standard.
journal: Nicotine & tobacco research : official journal of the Society for Research on Nicotine and Tobacco
abstract: The FDA proposed limiting nicotine in combustible cigarettes to ≤ 0.70 mg/g to reduce addictiveness. The tobacco industry has argued that such standards would render cigarettes functionally zero nicotine products, an interpretation industry contends exceeds the FDA's statutory authority. This study addresses this argument by extending existing evidence. It examined whether puffing a 0.4 mg/g very low nicotine content (VLNC) cigarette produced autonomic and cardiovascular responses distinct from a nicotine- and tobacco-free cigarette substitute (CS). Twenty-four adults who smoke took 8 puffs from a CS followed by a 0.4 mg/g cigarette. ECG (heart rate, RMSSD), the time-varying electrodermal activity index (TVSymp), and arterial stiffness (pulse wave velocity [PWV]) were recorded across pre-puffing, puffing, and post-puffing periods. Change scores from their respective pre-puffing (Δ) indicated that heart rate increased during puffing (Δ = 3.64 ± 4.26 bpm) and post-puffing (Δ = 2.66 ± 2.80 bpm; Ps < .001 vs. CS). RMSSD decreased during puffing (Δ = -0.14 ± 2.67 ms; P = .03 vs. CS) and post-puffing (Δ = -1.21 ± 2.40 ms; P = .04 vs. CS). TVSymp increased during puffing (Δ = 0.67 ± 0.47; P < .001 vs. CS) and post-puffing (Δ = 0.64 ± 0.47; P = .002 vs. CS). Post-puffing PWV increased (Δ = +0.47 ± 0.69 m/s; P = .004 vs. CS). Smoking 0.4 mg/g cigarette produced measurable autonomic and cardiovascular effects. These findings inform ongoing regulatory discussions and indicate that VLNC cigarettes are not functionally equivalent to "zero nicotine" products.

title: Invasive and Transcutaneous Vagus Nerve Stimulation for Upper-Limb Recovery After Stroke: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis of Randomized Controlled Trials.
journal: Neuromodulation : journal of the International Neuromodulation Society
abstract: Stroke is a leading cause of long-term disability, with upper-limb impairment being common and debilitating. Vagus nerve stimulation (VNS) is a promising therapy to improve neuroplasticity and motor recovery after stroke. However, comparative evidence for invasive VNS (iVNS) and transcutaneous VNS (taVNS) is limited. We conducted a systematic review and meta-analysis to assess their efficacy and safety in upper-limb rehabilitation. A systematic literature search of PubMed, Embase, and Scopus was performed. Randomized controlled trials evaluating VNS paired with rehabilitation in adult patients with ischemic or hemorrhagic stroke were included. The primary outcome was upper-limb motor recovery assessed using the Fugl-Meyer Assessment-Upper Extremity. Secondary outcomes included the Wolf Motor Function Test, the Modified Barthel Index, and adverse events. A total of 11 randomized controlled trials comprising 402 patients were included. VNS was associated with significant improvement in Fugl-Meyer Assessment-Upper Extremity scores compared with control groups (mean difference [MD], 4.45; 95% CI, 2.49-6.40; p < 0.00001), although substantial heterogeneity was observed (I2 = 93%). Sensitivity analysis showed persistent treatment effects with markedly reduced heterogeneity (MD, 2.73; 95% CI, 1.99-3.48; I2 = 4%). Significant improvements also were observed for Wolf Motor Function Test (MD, 1.40; 95% CI, 0.56-2.25) and Modified Barthel Index (MD, 6.57; 95% CI, 2.02-11.11). Subgroup analyses showed significant benefits for both invasive and transcutaneous VNS compared with their respective control groups, with no statistically significant differences between the subgroup estimates. However, these findings should not be interpreted as evidence of equivalence between delivery modalities because no direct head-to-head comparisons were available. The overall adverse-event risk did not significantly differ between VNS and control groups (odds ratio, 2.52; 95% CI, 0.85-7.48). However, device-related adverse events showed a borderline increase among patients treated with VNS (odds ratio, 2.35; 95% CI, 1.01-5.46), although this estimate was based on relatively few events. Most taVNS-related adverse events were mild and transient, whereas iVNS studies showed procedure-related complications, including pain, bruising, hoarseness, and vocal cord paresis. VNS combined with rehabilitation significantly improves post stroke upper-limb recovery. Both invasive and transcutaneous methods are effective, but taVNS is more scalable and less invasive because it avoids surgery and device implantation procedures. More multicenter trials are necessary to determine the long-term efficacy, safety, and optimal clinical use of VNS in stroke rehabilitation.

title: Prediction of Acetaminophen-Induced Hepatotoxicity in Acetylcysteine-Treated Patients Using Routine Admission Biomarkers.
abstract: Some acetaminophen-overdose patients develop hepatotoxicity despite acetylcysteine treatment. Established tools struggle to prospectively identify subsequent toxicity. We developed a model using only routine admission biomarkers to identify acetylcysteine-treated patients at highest risk and compared it with the current benchmark, the acetaminophen-aminotransferase multiplication product (AT product). Retrospective cohort study of acetaminophen overdose admissions aged 12 years and older (International Classification of Diseases 10th revision code of T39.1) with alanine aminotransferase (ALT) ≤1,000 U/L at admission from 3 UK hospitals (2008-2024). We fitted elastic-net logistic models stratified by presentation ALT. The outcome was peak ALT >1,000 U/L. Performance was assessed on a 25% held-out test set and benchmarked against the AT product >1,500. Of 4,705 admissions, 119 (2.5%) developed hepatotoxicity. The model used 7 routine blood tests, 4 per stratum. At presentation, those with ALT ≤50 U/L, acetaminophen, sodium, potassium, and lymphocyte count remained in the model. In those with ALT 51 to 1,000 U/L at presentation, ALT, bilirubin, alkaline phosphatase, and lymphocyte count were used. In the test set (n=1,175), it achieved an area under the curve of 0.93 (95% confidence interval [CI] 0.89 to 0.97) versus 0.82 (0.72 to 0.91) for the AT product (paired difference 0.11; 95% CI 0.01 to 0.22; P=.03), with higher specificity and a higher positive likelihood ratio at every matched sensitivity. The model had a specificity of 82.5%, whereas an AT product > 1,500 had a specificity of 62.6%. The model positive likelihood ratio was 5.1 versus 2.4 for the AT product, with half the number of false-positive escalations (171 versus 365 per 1,000 patients). A stratified model using only routine admission biomarkers (the Edinburgh Risk Score) identifies acetylcysteine-treated patients at the highest residual hepatotoxicity risk, outperforming the AT product >1,500 across decision thresholds, supporting selection for intensified therapy.

title: Psychiatrists' Prescribing Choice Determinants for Brexpiprazole and Other Antipsychotics in Patients With Schizophrenia: Results From a National Congress-Based Survey in Argentina.
abstract: To characterize psychiatrists' self-reported antipsychotic prescribing practices when treating patients with schizophrenia, including clozapine and long-acting injectable antipsychotic (LAI) use and, specifically, awareness, use, and perceived barriers regarding brexpiprazole, a second-generation antipsychotic (SGA) newly introduced in Argentina. Cross-sectional, congress-based convenience survey of psychiatrists attending the International Congress of Psychiatry in Argentina. The survey assessed prescribers' characteristics, clinical practice, antipsychotic prescribing patterns for schizophrenia, awareness/use of brexpiprazole, and perceived treatment challenges. Multivariable backward elimination regression analyses examined factors associated with clinician-reported frequency of/any use of clozapine, LAIs and brexpiprazole. Among 371 psychiatrists (age = 38.7 ± 8.5 years; females = 60.1%), SGA prescribing predominated (80.3 ± 24.9%). Altogether, 12.8 ± 20.4% of the respondents' patients were prescribed clozapine and 11.6 ± 18.7% LAIs. Risperidone (30.8 ± 28.7%) and olanzapine (19.9 ± 22.6%) were most frequently prescribed, while brexpiprazole (3.9 ± 16.0%) was in the least prescribed group, together with lurasidone (3.8 ± 11.8%), cariprazine (3.3 ± 11.8%) and quetiapine (2.9 ± 10.5%). Altogether, only 29.1% of respondents reported prescribing brexpiprazole, citing limited availability, cost, and lack of experience as barriers. Across the complementary continuous and dichotomized prescribing analyses, a higher proportion of TRS patients and greater clinical exposure to patients with schizophrenia emerged as the factors most consistently associated with clozapine and LAI prescribing. Most important factors for selecting one antipsychotic over another were positive symptom efficacy (90.0%), tolerability (70.0%), negative symptom efficacy (64.7%) and lower cardiometabolic risk (54.9%). This national congress-based survey provides exploratory information regarding self-reported antipsychotic prescribing practices among participating Argentine psychiatrists and identifies several perceived challenges in the antipsychotic treatment of schizophrenia. The findings should be regarded as hypothesis-generating.

title: Organophosphate Flame Retardants Induce Neurodegenerative Pathologies by Paralyzing HSP90AB1 Chaperone Function: A Multi-Scale Computational and Biophysical Study.
abstract: This study integrated computational toxicology with biophysical and cellular validation to investigate the neurotoxic potential of 10 flame-retardant-related compounds. ADMETlab 3.0 predicted blood-brain barrier probabilities of 0.989 for bis(1,3-dichloro-2-propyl) phosphate and 0.444 for diphenyl phosphate (DPHP), interpreted as screening predictions. Network topology analysis identified HSP90AB1 as a shared candidate hub target linking organophosphate flame retardants to Alzheimer's and Parkinson's diseases. Molecular dynamics simulations indicated a stable HSP90AB1 backbone in the DPHP complex (root-mean-square deviation ∼0.18 nm). Surface plasmon resonance measured an equilibrium dissociation constant of 1.49 μM. DPHP induced dose-dependent cytotoxicity in neuronal cells; the half-maximal inhibitory concentration was not determined within the tested range. HSP90AB1 overexpression mitigated DPHP-induced reactive oxygen species production and transcriptional upregulation of pro-apoptotic and pro-inflammatory genes. Single-cell virtual knockout identified candidate regulatory processes; Parkinson's disease-related enrichment remained exploratory after multiple-testing correction. Together, the computational, biophysical, and cellular findings support HSP90AB1 as a candidate target of environmental neurotoxicity and motivate further investigation of DPHP.

title: Technological Substitution in Pesticide Application Reduces Occupational Risk but Fails to Mitigate Dietary Residue Burden: Field Evidence from UAV versus Manual Spraying in Paddy Rice.
abstract: UAV spraying has been widely promoted as superior to manual application in Asian rice production, yet its combined implications for food safety and occupational exposure have never been evaluated within a single integrated framework. Here, we report a full-season field trial comparing UAV and manual imidacloprid (IMI) application in paddy rice, simultaneously tracking grain residue dynamics and occupational exposure in 29 applicators through to harvest. Grain IMI concentrations at harvest were comparable between regimes (86-115 μg/kg) and exceeded the EU maximum residue limit (MRL, 10 μg/kg) in both groups. More critically, on an LC-HRMS-derived relative-concentration basis, parent IMI accounted for 30.4% of the detected IMI-related profile in grain, whereas transformation products collectively accounted for 69.6%. Among these, 6-hydroxynicotinic acid was the single highest-abundance compound, surpassing parent IMI itself, yet none of the detected transformation products are included in China's residue definition for imidacloprid in plant-derived foods. Regarding occupational exposure, urinary IMI rose approximately 9-fold from pre-exposure baseline in UAV operators compared with 17-fold in manual applicators. Manual application also induced markedly greater lipid peroxidation stress, with median baseline-normalized MDA fold changes of approximately 3.8- and 2.6-fold in the manual and UAV groups, respectively (p = 0.001). These findings establish that application technology substitution effectively reduces occupational exposure risk but confers no advantage at the food safety end point. Current parent-compound-centered residue surveillance frameworks systematically underestimate the true IMI-related burden in harvested grain, and expansion of regulatory monitoring beyond the parent compound is warranted.

title: Metatranscriptomics Reveals Potential Hybrid Electron Routing in Comammox Nitrospira and NO-Supplemented Cooperation in a Partial Nitritation-Anammox Bioreactor under Dynamic Aeration.
abstract: Intermittent aeration drives partial nitritation-anammox (PN-A) systems, yet how microbiomes regulate aerobic and anaerobic respiration during rapid, oxygen-limited redox shifts remains poorly understood. Here, we applied genome-resolved metatranscriptomics to evaluate transcriptional dynamics in a long-term PN-A bioreactor treating low concentrations of ammonium. Under intermittent aeration, active populations did not follow strict metabolic switching, but instead exhibited complementary regulation by coordinately transcribing aerobic and anaerobic respiratory pathways. Notably, comammox Nitrospira exhibited a severe transcriptional bottleneck, with terminal oxidase expression 2-3 orders of magnitude lower than that of amo and nirK. Gene coexpression and pathway mapping support a novel hybrid electron transport chain where electrons from ammonia oxidation are directly routed to nirK. This alternative electron-transfer route functionally couples energy dissipation with obligatory nitrite detoxification. Concurrently, a severe transcriptional deficit of nirS relative to hdh in anammox Ca. Kuenenia indicates a partial bypass of intracellular nitrite reduction. Collectively, these patterns support a novel nitric oxide-supplemented cooperation: anammox bacteria scavenge extracellular nitric oxide generated by comammox Nitrospira, conserving their own electrons while acting as a vital sink to relieve comammox nitric oxide toxicity. These findings provide a mechanistic blueprint for optimizing advanced PN-A microbiomes through engineered aeration control.

title: The Role of Affective Traits and Social Cognition in Envy and Schadenfreude.
abstract: Complex social emotions like envy and Schadenfreude challenge traditional models of social cognition by revealing how affective traits interact with cognitive processes to shape counter-empathic responses. Although theoretically linked to empathy and theory of mind (ToM), their associations with traits like alexithymia and anhedonia remain underexplored. This study tested a structural model connecting affective traits (alexithymia, anhedonia), social cognition (ToM, empathy), and social emotions (envy, Schadenfreude) in 125 healthy adults using validated measures and structural equation modeling. Results showed that alexithymia indirectly influenced empathy and envy via reduced ToM, while empathy did not directly predict these emotions. Alexithymia correlated positively with anhedonia and negatively with ToM. Anhedonia predicted lower empathy. Envy strongly predicted Schadenfreude, underscoring the role of upward social comparison. Findings suggest that these emotions arise from distinct affective and cognitive mechanisms, offering a novel framework for understanding socio-emotional functioning in both healthy and clinical populations.

title: Structural Differences Associated With Chess Expertise: Fusiform Regional Mean MIND Similarity and White Matter Diffusion Differences.
abstract: Chess expertise has been associated with differences in brain structure and function, yet its structural characteristics remain incompletely understood. This study aimed to characterize cortical morphometric and white matter diffusion differences in professional chess players and to evaluate the discriminative performance of imaging features. A total of 58 participants (29 professional chess players and 29 novices) were included from the 1000 Functional Connectomes Project. High-resolution T1-weighted MRI and diffusion tensor imaging data were analyzed to extract cortical morphometric measures, regional mean Morphometric INverse Divergence (MIND) similarity, and white matter diffusion metrics. A logistic regression model was developed using regional mean MIND similarity and FA and MD measures and evaluated across 100 repeated stratified train-test splits. Feature selection and model optimization were performed exclusively within the training set. Model performance was assessed using AUC and Brier score. Among the five cortical morphometric measures, cortical thickness showed significant differences in 19 cortical regions between professional chess players and novices after false discovery rate (FDR) correction. Cortical thickness was lower in professional chess players in all 19 regions. Regional mean MIND similarity analysis revealed that professional chess players showed higher regional mean MIND similarity in the left fusiform gyrus than novices. Professional chess players also showed higher FA in the left cingulum (hippocampus). Higher MD was observed in the fornix, right anterior limb of the internal capsule, and right superior corona radiata. Across 100 repeated stratified train-test splits, the model achieved a mean AUC of 0.739 (SD = 0.118) and a mean Brier score of 0.238 (SD = 0.066). Professional chess players showed distinct cortical morphometric and white matter diffusion characteristics compared with novices. These differences particularly involved the left fusiform gyrus and white matter pathways related to memory and cognitive control. The imaging-based model showed moderate discriminative ability. These findings provide evidence for structural brain differences associated with chess expertise.

title: A Framework for Collaborative Advancement: Consensus Priorities From the Cancer Cachexia Society Paediatric Network Workshop.
journal: Journal of cachexia, sarcopenia and muscle
abstract: Cancer cachexia represents a complex and multifactorial syndrome of muscle- and fat-loss related to inflammation and metabolic alterations and a hypercatabolic state in response to cancer and cancer-directed therapies. The Fearon Criteria, the most widely cited criteria for cachexia in adults, raised attention for the need to improve mechanisms driving cachexia and potential therapeutic targets. Despite more than a decade since publication, paediatric cancer cachexia remains largely ill-defined and understudied. To address the critical need to understand the similarities and differences between adult and childhood cancer cachexia, the Cancer Cachexia Society convened a meeting of multidisciplinary experts to define the state of understanding of childhood cancer cachexia, knowledge gaps in the basic, clinical and translational research and clarify future priorities for clinical care and research of childhood cancer cachexia. The workshop created a consensus document outlining future directions in the following domains: malnutrition screening and assessment, body composition measures and modalities, mechanisms of paediatric cancer cachexia, patient-reported outcomes and quality of life, defining paediatric cancer cachexia and trial implications and creating a paediatric clinical-trial framework. Additionally, focused discussions explored needs for considerations of patient perspective and patient advocacy, engaging trainees, disseminating work and expanding cachexia research to survivorship and resource limited settings. The group concluded the highest priorities should include establishing paediatric-specific diagnostic criteria for cachexia, creating and leveraging a measurement infrastructure that applies across routine clinical care and clinical research, specifically focusing on age-specific molecular pathways and drivers of childhood cachexia to advocate for specific childhood focused clinical trials. Our consensus is that patients, families and global partners must be engaged with basic, clinical and translational researchers to specifically advance childhood cancer cachexia care. The Cancer Cachexia Society remains dedicated to this mission and will leverage these recommendations to create a Paediatric Cancer Cachexia Network with the specific mission of prioritizing a better treatment for children with cancer and ultimately improve the survival and morbidity for children with cancer.

title: Hemorrhage Risk in Unruptured Brain Arteriovenous Malformations before and after Stereotactic Radiosurgery.
abstract: Background Whether stereotactic radiosurgery (SRS) is associated with lower hemorrhage risk for unruptured brain arteriovenous malformations (AVMs) during the latency period (ie, from SRS to complete AVM obliteration) remains controversial. Purpose To evaluate whether SRS is associated with lower hemorrhage risk in unruptured brain AVMs during the latency period when analyzed from the time of diagnosis. Materials and Methods This single-center retrospective study included 511 patients with unruptured brain AVMs at diagnosis treated with single-session SRS between June 1990 and May 2024. Hemorrhage rates before and after SRS were calculated using the person-year method. A time-dependent Cox proportional hazards model was used to assess the association between SRS and hemorrhage risk. The pre-SRS hemorrhage rate was calculated using the interval between diagnosis and SRS. Results For the 511 patients (median age, 39 years [IQR, 28-52 years]; 306 male patients), the total observation period from diagnosis to SRS or any prior treatment was 1009 person-years, and the pre-SRS hemorrhage rate was 3.4 per 100 person-years (34 hemorrhages). Among 477 patients who underwent SRS without a pre-SRS hemorrhage, 75 patients were lost to follow-up during the latency period, and the median latency period was 33 months, with a total of 1711 person-years. Hemorrhage occurred in 24 patients during the latency period, yielding an overall latency-period hemorrhage rate of 1.4 per 100 person-years. After adjustment for age, nidus volume, and venous drainage, time-dependent Cox proportional hazards analysis showed that SRS was associated with lower hemorrhage risk in the post-SRS latency period compared with the pre-SRS period, corresponding to a 53% lower hazard (adjusted hazard ratio, 0.47 [95% CI: 0.27, 0.83]; P = .009). SRS was also associated with lower hemorrhage risk in lesions treated with SRS following prior surgery or endovascular therapy (hazard ratio, 0.20; P = .01). Conclusion In patients with unruptured brain AVMs, SRS was associated with lower hemorrhage risk during the latency period when analyzed from the time of diagnosis. © RSNA, 2026 Supplemental material is available for this article.

title: Ferroelectric Neuromorphic Devices Enable Nonphotosensitive Neurons to Achieve Event-Driven Photosensitive Artificial Neural Interfaces.
abstract: Neuromorphic devices integrated with biological neurons hold significant potential for rehabilitation and human-machine interfaces, thereby attracting extensive research interest. However, the effort to connect them through light stimulation is still in its very initial stages. Here, ferroelectric neuromorphic devices based on α-In2Se3 and P(VDF-TrFE) are proposed to construct hybrid neural interfaces. In contrast to neuromorphic devices employing other working principles, ferroelectricity plays a crucial role in connecting biological neurons, which enables nonphotosensitive neurons to respond to light stimuli. Various optoelectronic synaptic behaviors have been achieved. Under light pulses, the ferroelectric neuromorphic device induced a significant increase of up to 200% in the calcium ion signal of artificial neural interfaces. Patch-clamp was applied for further verification, revealing the influence of different light wavelengths and pulse frequencies on neuronal excitation signals, which is analogous to the human retina. Simulations demonstrate that the ferroelectric neural interface improves dynamic gesture recognition accuracy from 51% to 99%. Our approach offers a strategy to connect neuromorphic devices with neurons through light, which may offer a platform to investigate the fundamental principles of synaptic plasticity and learning in a hybrid setting for future remote therapy and human-machine interfaces.

title: Chronic Stress-Triggerable Nanoprodrugs Ameliorate Metabolic Abnormalities Driven by Hypothalamic-Pituitary-Adrenal Axis Dysregulation in Early Alzheimer's Disease.
abstract: Chronic stress-induced dysregulation of the hypothalamic-pituitary-adrenal (HPA) axis is a crucial early risk factor that triggers brain energy metabolism disorders to accelerate the onset and progression of Alzheimer's disease (AD). Herein, an amphiphilic precursor conjugate of ginsenoside Rc (Rc) covalently linked with a reactive oxygen species-sensitive thioketo bond is constructed to form stimuli-responsive prodrug assemblies, which are further modified with the TGN-Tet1 dual-ligand fusion peptide TPL to obtain a chronic stress-triggerable programmed nanoprodrug (TLRN). Following TPL-mediated blood-brain barrier penetration and neuronal preferential targeting, nanoprodrugs specifically disintegrate to selectively release active Rc in the chronic stress-induced excessive reactive oxygen species (ROS) microenvironment. Benefiting from the restoration of HPA axis homeostasis by normalizing glucocorticoid receptor nuclear translocation, TLRN treatment exhibits multifaceted rectification of cerebral metabolic abnormalities, including enhancing glucose uptake, promoting oxidative phosphorylation, and mitigating mitochondrial dysfunction. In young amyloid precursor protein/presenilin 1 (APP/PS1) transgenic mouse models exposed to chronic stress, this intervention can alleviate brain energy deprivation and amyloid-β (Aβ) accumulation, ultimately rescuing depressive-like behaviors and cognitive deficits, offering a promising approach for early prevention and flexible management of AD at high risk of chronic stress.

title: Polarization-Controlled Dual-Mode Switching in van der Waals α-In2Se3 Memristors for Multitime-Scale Reservoir Computing.
abstract: Electrochemical-metallization (ECM) memristors can implement both nonvolatile memory switching and volatile threshold switching, making them attractive for neuromorphic and reservoir computing; however, the stochastic formation of metallic filaments causes variability in the threshold voltage and switching instability. Here, we report a van der Waals α-In2Se3-based ferroelectric-semiconductor ECM (FeS-ECM) memristor in which a bidirectionally polarized α-In2Se3 layer is inserted between the inert electrode and the switching layer. The out-of-plane ferroelectric polarization, programmed through a decoupled in-plane poling terminal, deterministically selects within the low-compliance operating regime between nonvolatile bipolar memory switching and volatile unipolar threshold switching within a single device, with a coefficient of variation in the set voltage of 4.7% and stable operation over more than 9000 cycles. Exploiting these two modes, a single α-In2Se3 platform exhibits both the volatile reservoir dynamics and the nonvolatile conductance modulation required for the readout weights of a physical reservoir-computing system, in which the pulse width electrically programs multiple relaxation time constants. This pulse-width multitime scale reconfigurability enables efficient temporal information processing, demonstrated through MNIST classification and chaotic time-series prediction.

title: Decoupling Conductivity and Interfacial State in Pristine-Like Carbon Nanotube Coatings Reveals Their Distinct Contributions to Neuronal Function.
abstract: Carbon nanotubes (CNTs) combine high electrical conductivity, mechanical robustness, and nanoscale architecture, making them promising materials for neural interfaces. However, the strong coupling between CNT morphology, electrical transport, and surface chemistry has limited identification of the material properties that directly regulate neuronal function. Here, we establish an experimental strategy to disentangle morphology-dependent network transport from interfacial wettability using pristine-like CNT coatings. Multiwalled CNTs with comparable diameters but distinct lengths were reversibly functionalized, spray-coated, and thermally defunctionalized to produce homogeneous conductive networks while recovering pristine-like electrical transport and surface chemistry. Subsequent conditioning in phosphate-buffered saline substantially reduced surface hydrophobicity without detectable alteration of the graphitic CNT framework, generating coatings with comparable interfacial wettability but distinct network morphologies. Primary spinal cord neuron-glia cultures grown on these substrates were characterized by immunocytochemistry, electrophysiology, and calcium imaging. All CNT coatings supported comparable neuroglial density and network formation, whereas PBS-conditioned coatings, characterized by a more wettable interface, consistently exhibited enhanced spontaneous bursting and calcium activity compared with their untreated coatings. Across all conditions, neuronal network activity was more consistently associated with the initial interfacial state of CNT coatings, as experimentally reflected by their wetting behavior, than with CNT length or morphology-dependent electrical transport. These findings identify the initial CNT interfacial state, with wettability serving as an experimentally accessible descriptor, as a key design parameter for CNT-based neural interfaces. Furthermore, they suggest that the initial interfacial state may influence the subsequent evolution of the biomolecular layer at the cell-facing interface, thereby contributing to the modulation of neuronal function.

title: An Optoelectronic SnP2S6 Memristive Neuron for Biologically Inspired Multimodal Neuromorphic Information Processing.
abstract: Neuromorphic systems capable of integrating multiple sensory modalities offer a promising route toward energy-efficient information processing that more closely emulates biological neural networks. Here, we demonstrate a multifunctional ITO/SnP2S6/Ti memristive neuron that combines reproducible volatile resistive switching and integrate-and-fire dynamics under electrical-pulse stimulation with wavelength-selective photoresponses and short-term optoelectronic synaptic plasticity. Leveraging these experimentally measured device characteristics, we construct a multimodal neuromorphic recognition framework that integrates volatile memristive neurons with programmable memristive synapses. Inspired by the parallel processing of visual features in the primate visual system, structural and color information are independently encoded and processed through separate electrical and optical pathways before being integrated for classification. Importantly, inference is implemented using experimentally measured neuronal firing statistics and programmed synaptic conductance states, rather than idealized device models, thereby establishing a direct link between device characteristics and system-level functionality. As a proof-of-concept, the framework is evaluated on a fruit-recognition task using a subset of the Fruits-360 image data set, achieving a classification accuracy of 94.9% through multimodal fusion and substantially outperforming recognition based on either modality alone. These results establish SnP2S6 memristive devices as a versatile platform for integrating electrical and optical neuronal functionalities and highlight their potential for hardware-realistic multimodal in-sensor neuromorphic computing.

title: A Flexible Complementary Memristive Synapse for Convolutional Neural Network Applications.
abstract: The memristive artificial synapse, which typically operates on the basis of various filamentary conductance-update mechanisms, has been extensively utilized to implement hardware neural networks for brain-inspired computing. However, the stochastic conductance-switching characteristics that arise from uncontrollable filamentary evolution within the two-terminal device have long hindered hardware neural networks from achieving training and recognition performance comparable to their software neural network. Here, we propose a flexible complementary memristive synapse that achieves highly linear conductance-update behavior while preserving a large dynamic range. This synapse consists of a homogeneous bilayer of two amorphous indium-gallium-tin oxide (a-IGTO) films deposited under different oxygen partial pressures: an oxygen-deficient, VO-rich layer formed without O2 supply and an oxygen-supplied, VO-poor layer formed with O2 supply, exhibiting incremental and decremental conductance-update behaviors, respectively. The distinct oxygen-vacancy-related states and filament-evolution characteristics of the two layers suggest vacancy-mediated layer-to-layer redistribution, which can mutually compensate the nonideal conductive filament evolution of the two different layers, thereby facilitating more gradual modulation of the net conductance. The proposed flexible synapse exhibits robust mechanical stability and durability after 12,000 bending-release cycles, as confirmed by electrical characterization while maintained in the bent state at a bending radius of 2 mm. Finally, the applicability of the proposed flexible synapses to HW-NNs is evaluated through a VGG-8-based CIFAR-10 image recognition simulation using experimentally measured synaptic characteristics for weight updates in the two fully connected layers.

title: Low-Threshold Intermittent Hypoxia Exacerbates LPS-Induced Depressive-Like Behaviors and Cognitive Deficits While Potentiating the Hippocampal STING-TBK1 Pathway.
abstract: Depressive disorders and cognitive impairment are debilitating neuropsychiatric conditions often driven by chronic neuroinflammation. Although systemic inflammation induced by lipopolysaccharide (LPS) is a standard model for investigating these pathologies, evidence suggests that hypoxic environments also trigger immune activation. In this study, we sought to determine whether low-threshold intermittent hypoxia exacerbates LPS-induced depressive-like behaviors and cognitive deficits and to identify the potential underlying molecular mechanisms. Adult male mice were exposed to low-threshold intermittent hypoxia during a systemic LPS challenge. Depressive-like phenotypes were evaluated through the tail suspension test, forced swim test, and sucrose preference test. Cognitive function was assessed via the Morris water maze test. Following behavioral testing, the expression levels of proteins related to the STING-TBK1-IRF3 signaling pathway and the synaptic markers postsynaptic density protein 95 (PSD-95) and synaptophysin (SYN) were quantified in the hippocampus. Additionally, hippocampal concentrations of the pro-inflammatory cytokines interleukin-1 beta, interleukin-6, and tumor necrosis factor-alpha were measured. LPS administration successfully induced depressive-like behaviors and cognitive decline in adult mice. Notably, low-threshold intermittent hypoxia significantly amplified these LPS-induced behavioral aberrations, despite being insufficient to elicit such impairments independently. Molecular analysis revealed that low-threshold intermittent hypoxia further intensified the activation of the STING-TBK1 innate immune pathway and exacerbated the downregulation of PSD-95 and SYN expression in the hippocampus of LPS-treated mice. These changes were accompanied by a robust elevation of pro-inflammatory cytokine levels. Our findings demonstrated that low-threshold intermittent hypoxia exacerbates LPS-induced depressive-like behaviors, cognitive dysfunction, and neuroinflammation. This synergistic deterioration is likely associated with the hyperactivation of the STING-dependent innate immune response and reduced expression of hippocampal synaptic markers.

title: ODC1-Mediated Polyamine Dysregulation Promotes Retinal Neurodegeneration in Alzheimer's Disease by Impairing Autophagy-Lysosomal Homeostasis.
abstract: Alzheimer's disease (AD) involves significant retinal pathology, but the underlying metabolic mechanisms remain unclear. Polyamine metabolism regulates neuronal and glial homeostasis, yet its role in the AD retina is unknown. We identified ornithine decarboxylase 1 (ODC1)-mediated polyamine dysregulation as a metabolic mechanism linking Müller glial dysfunction to impaired autophagy and retinal neurodegeneration in AD. Retinal polyamine levels and ODC1 expression were examined in AD retinas. ODC1 inhibition was achieved using α-difluoromethylornithine (DFMO) in vivo and small interfering RNA (siRNA) knockdown in human Müller glial cells. Retinal structure and function were assessed by histology, electroretinography, and visual behavior tests. Transcriptomic profiling, western blotting, and immunofluorescence evaluated autophagy-lysosomal homeostasis. Exogenous putrescine confirmed the metabolic specificity of ODC1-driven effects. The 5XFAD mouse retinas showed ODC1 upregulation, increased putrescine, reduced spermidine and spermine, and enhanced gliosis markers. Intravitreal Aβ1-42 induced sustained ODC1 expression, whereas DFMO suppressed inflammation, preserved retinal thickness, enhanced electroretinography, and improved visual behaviors. Transcriptomic and biochemical analyses revealed that DFMO enhanced lysosomal- and autophagy-related transcriptional programs, with lysosomal-associated membrane protein 1 (LAMP1) restoration, p62 reduction, and LC3II/I normalization. In Müller cells, Odc1 knockdown attenuated Aβ-induced reactive changes, preserved lysosomal activity, and normalized autophagy signaling. Exogenous putrescine reversed these effects, confirming a functional link between ODC1-driven putrescine accumulation and autophagy-lysosomal dysfunction. Dysregulated polyamine metabolism drives retinal degeneration in AD. ODC1-mediated putrescine accumulation links Müller glial activation to impaired autophagy-lysosomal homeostasis, defective Aβ clearance, neuronal loss, and visual dysfunction. Targeting ODC1 with DFMO may represent a therapeutic strategy to preserve retinal structure and visual function in AD.

title: A Phase 2 Study of Imlifidase in the Treatment of Guillain-Barré Syndrome.
abstract: Guillain-Barré syndrome (GBS), a life-threatening neuropathy, results in prolonged disability despite standard-of-care treatment. Imlifidase specifically cleaves immunoglobulin G (IgG) antibodies and may benefit patients with GBS by rapidly depleting pathologic IgG autoantibodies, resulting in less severe disease and faster recovery. This open-label, single-arm, multicenter, phase 2 study enrolled adults with severe GBS (i.e., GBS disability scale [GBS-DS] grades ranging from 3 to 5; GBS-DS grades range from 0 to 6, with higher numbers indicating more severe disability). It investigated safety, adverse event profile, efficacy, pharmacodynamics, and pharmacokinetics of one dose of imlifidase within 12 days of symptom onset followed by standard-dose intravenous immune globulin (IVIG). Twenty-seven participants with confirmed GBS were assessed by using standard GBS outcome measures, including GBS-DS and the Medical Research Council sum score (scores range from 0 to 60, with a lower score indicting more severe weakness). Median (95% confidence interval) time to improve at least one GBS-DS grade was 6 (3.0 to 16.0) days, and time to independent walking was 16 (4.0 to 92.0) days. Within 1 week, 37% of patients were able to walk independently, and the mean improvement in the Medical Research Council sum score was 10.7 points. Twenty-five participants (83%) experienced at least one treatment-emergent adverse event. Most were grade 1 (mild) or grade 2 (moderate). Five were assessed as being grade 3 (severe) and two events as being grade 4 (life-threatening or disabling intensity), including one death. A single dose of imlifidase followed by IVIG in participants with severe GBS was associated with rapid functional improvements. These results support a randomized controlled trial to further investigate IgG-depleting strategies in GBS. (ClinicalTrials.gov number, NCT03943589.).

title: Sildenafil for Fetal Growth Restriction - An Individual Participant Meta-Analysis.
abstract: Phosphodiesterase type-5 inhibitors have been investigated as an in utero therapy for fetal growth restriction (FGR). We conducted a systematic review and individual participant data meta-analysis of randomized trials of phosphodiesterase type-5 inhibitors versus placebo/no treatment in singleton pregnancies with FGR. The primary outcome was infant survival without serious adverse outcome. Secondary outcomes included gestation at birth and birth weight z score among liveborn infants. Predefined subgroups were evaluated. Of 19 eligible trials, 4 contributed data. Of 492 participants, 240 had been assigned to placebo and 252 to the phosphodiesterase type-5 inhibitor sildenafil. Infant survival without serious adverse outcome occurred in 110 of 240 participants (45.8%) assigned to placebo versus 113 of 252 participants (44.8%) assigned to sildenafil (relative risk [RR], 0.96; 95% confidence interval [CI], 0.78 to 1.17). No apparent interaction was observed between subgroups. There was no apparent difference in gestation at birth (mean difference -0.5 weeks; 95% CI, -1.3 to 0.2) or birth weight z score (mean difference, 0.0; 95% CI, -0.2 to 0.2). Persistent pulmonary hypertension of the newborn occurred in 10 of 176 participants (5.7%) assigned to placebo versus 27 of 197 participants (13.7%) assigned to sildenafil (RR, 2.39; 95% CI, 1.23 to 4.61); nitric oxide was used in 15 of 176 participants (8.5%) assigned to placebo versus 20 of 197 participants (10.2%) assigned to sildenafil (RR, 1.21; 95% CI, 0.64 to 2.29). Maternal sildenafil therapy for FGR was not associated with improved outcomes for infants. It was associated with persistent pulmonary hypertension of the newborn but not with an increase in nitric oxide therapy. (Funded by Health Research Council of New Zealand and others; PROSPERO number, CRD42017069688; ANZCTR number, ACTRN12612000584831; ISRCTN number, ISRCTN39133303; ClinicalTrials.gov numbers, NCT02442492 and NCT02277132.).

title: The Lung-Brain-Immune Axis: Mechanistic Pathways Linking Pulmonary Inflammation to Neuropsychiatric and Neurological Disease.
abstract: Chronic respiratory diseases and neuropsychiatric and neurological disorders contribute substantially to the global disease burden but have traditionally been studied as distinct organ-system disorders. Emerging evidence supports an integrated lung-brain-immune axis through which pulmonary inflammation can alter central nervous system (CNS) function and contribute to neurological and neuropsychiatric disease. This review synthesizes preclinical and clinical literature examining the anatomical, immunological, environmental, and clinical mechanisms linking pulmonary inflammation to CNS dysfunction. Evidence was synthesized across neural and immune communication pathways, inflammatory signaling, environmental and infectious triggers, disease-specific associations, lifespan susceptibility, and translational applications. Lung-brain communication is bidirectional and occurs through vagal and autonomic neural pathways, circulating inflammatory mediators including interleukin (IL)-1β, IL-6, and tumor necrosis factor (TNF)-α, immune-cell trafficking, and disruption of the alveolar-capillary and blood-brain barriers. These processes promote microglial priming, astrocyte reactivity, oxidative stress, and synaptic dysfunction, providing a cellular basis for cognitive and affective symptoms. Air pollution, respiratory viruses, allergens, and tobacco smoke can activate these pathways, which are implicated in asthma, chronic obstructive pulmonary disease, acute respiratory distress syndrome, long COVID, and interstitial lung disease. Susceptibility varies across the lifespan, from prenatal immune activation and adolescence to immunosenescence. Emerging biomarkers, anti-inflammatory and neuromodulatory therapies, and immune-phenotype-based stratification may enable more targeted interventions. The lung-brain-immune axis provides a unifying biological framework in which pulmonary inflammation can act as a modifiable driver of neuroimmune dysfunction. Mechanistically validated causal models and longitudinal human studies are needed to clarify disease-specific pathways and translate these insights into clinical practice.

title: Emerging biomarkers of multiple sclerosis activity and progression: current status, challenges, and future perspectives.
journal: Critical reviews in clinical laboratory sciences
abstract: Multiple sclerosis (MS) is a chronic central nervous system disorder characterized by complex pathobiology involving overlapping immune-mediated inflammation and progressive neurodegeneration, both contributing to cumulative disability. Despite substantial advances in MS research and management, reliable biomarkers capable of capturing disease activity, progression, and therapeutic response remain an important unmet need. This review critically synthesizes current evidence on biomarkers reflecting immune activation, neuroaxonal injury, glial dysfunction, oxidative stress, and molecular and metabolic alterations. Among currently investigated fluid biomarkers, neurofilament light chain is the most extensively validated marker of neuroaxonal injury and inflammatory disease activity, whereas glial fibrillary acidic protein provides complementary information on astrocytic pathology and disease progression. Emerging approaches based on lipidomics and metabolomics, extracellular vesicles, transcriptomic and epigenetic profiling, microRNAs, and gut microbiome-associated signatures may further improve characterization of relapsing and progressive MS. Experimental models are considered as complementary translational platforms for linking measurable biomarker changes with defined mechanisms of inflammation, tissue injury, metabolic dysfunction, and treatment response, while distinguishing mechanistic plausibility from clinical biomarker performance. Given the biological heterogeneity of MS, future progress is likely to depend on integrated, multi-compartment and multi-omic biomarker signatures combined with clinical and imaging measures rather than on individual markers alone. Large longitudinal cohorts, analytical standardization, independent validation, and assessment across MS phenotypes and treatment settings will be essential for translating these approaches into clinically useful tools for monitoring disease activity and progression, prognosis, patient stratification, and individualized management.

title: Moonlighting Roles of Serine Protease Inhibitors in Immune Homeostasis and Diseases.
abstract: Serpins a conserved superfamily of serine protease inhibitors, regulate proteolytic cascades in coagulation, fibrinolysis, complement activation and inflammation via a suicide-substrate mechanism ensuring immune and tissue homeostasis. Beyond this canonical function, recent studies reveal "moonlighting" functions in cell signalling, extracellular matrix remodelling, immune cell activation, cancer progression, and host-pathogen interactions. In tumours, serpins function contextually to either restrain growth by curbing inflammation and proteolysis or promote tumour progression through effects on angiogenesis, metastasis, and therapy resistance. In infectious diseases, both host-derived and pathogen-encoded serpins influence pathogen survival, immune evasion, and inflammatory damage. Emerging evidence indicates that the serpin role is highly context dependent, shaped by cellular source, tissue environment, and disease state. Advances in structural biology and protein engineering have begun to clarify mechanisms governing serpin specificity, stability, and regulatory plasticity. We review these recent developments and outline key principles by which serpins regulate immune homeostasis, tumour biology, host-pathogen dynamics, and discuss how these insights position serpins as promising targets in cancer, infectious diseases, and immune-mediated disorders.
